prompt: How many casual leaves can I take in a year?
chosen: Full-time employees are entitled to 12 days of casual leave per calendar year. Casual leave is meant for short, unplanned absences and can be taken in half-day or full-day increments. It cannot be carried forward to the next year and unused balance lapses on December 31st. Apply through the HR portal with at least 24 hours advance notice for planned casual leave.
rejected: You get some casual leaves. Check with HR about the exact number.

prompt: Can I take sick leave without a medical certificate?
chosen: Yes, sick leave of 1-2 consecutive days does not require a medical certificate. However, if sick leave exceeds 2 consecutive days (3 or more days), a medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner must be submitted upon return to work. Submit the certificate to HR within 2 days of resuming duties. Frequent single-day sick leaves may trigger a wellness check-in.
rejected: I think you need a certificate for all sick leaves. Better ask someone.

prompt: What happens to my leave balance if I resign mid-year?
chosen: Upon resignation, your earned leave balance is encashed at your Basic Pay rate as part of the full and final settlement. Casual leave and sick leave are not encashable. Leave entitlement for the year is prorated based on your actual working months. For example, if you resign after 6 months, your entitlement is calculated as half the annual allocation minus leave already taken.
rejected: Your leaves will be adjusted when you leave.

prompt: How do I apply for maternity leave?
chosen: Apply for maternity leave through the HR portal under Leave Management > Special Leave > Maternity Leave. Submit the application along with a medical certificate confirming expected delivery date at least 8 weeks before the due date. You are entitled to 26 weeks of paid maternity leave for the first two children. The leave can begin up to 8 weeks before the expected delivery. Contact your HR Business Partner for a detailed walkthrough of the process.
rejected: Just apply for leave on the portal. HR will handle it.

prompt: Can I take leave during my probation period?
chosen: Yes, leave is available during probation. Your leave entitlement is prorated from your joining date. Casual leave, sick leave, and earned leave accrue proportionally. However, it is advisable to use leave judiciously during probation as attendance and commitment are evaluation criteria. Unapproved absences during probation may affect your confirmation decision.
rejected: Probably not. Wait until you're confirmed.

prompt: What is the maximum number of consecutive days I can take off?
chosen: For earned leave, you can take up to 15 consecutive working days (3 weeks) with prior approval from your manager, submitted at least 7 days in advance. Leave exceeding 15 days requires department head approval and a handover plan. For special circumstances (medical, family emergency), extended leave can be approved on a case-by-case basis by HR.
rejected: There's a limit on leaves. Ask your manager about it.

prompt: Is loss of pay (LOP) applied if I exhaust all my leaves?
chosen: Yes, once all leave types (casual, sick, and earned leave) are exhausted, any additional absence is marked as Loss of Pay (LOP). LOP is deducted from your monthly salary on a per-day basis (monthly salary / 30). LOP also affects your provident fund contribution and may impact performance ratings if excessive. Always plan leave utilization carefully throughout the year.
rejected: If you don't have leaves, salary gets cut I guess.

prompt: Can I cancel an approved leave?
chosen: Yes, approved leave can be cancelled through the HR portal before the leave start date. Navigate to Leave Management > My Leaves > Cancel Request. Cancellations made on or after the leave start date require manager re-approval. Cancelled leave days are restored to your balance immediately. For partially availed leave, submit an early return notification to update records.
rejected: You can probably cancel it. Try the system.

prompt: Why is my salary lower than expected this month?
chosen: Salary differences can occur due to several factors: income tax (TDS) adjustments based on updated declarations, professional tax deduction, LOP days in the current month, insurance premium changes during annual enrollment, provident fund contribution adjustments, or recovery of salary advance installments. Check your detailed payslip on the HR portal under My Documents > Payslips for a line-by-line breakdown of earnings and deductions.
rejected: Sometimes salary varies. You can check your payslip.

prompt: When do I get my annual bonus?
chosen: Annual bonus is typically disbursed in April for the previous financial year's performance. The bonus is calculated based on three factors: individual performance rating (40% weight), team/department performance (30% weight), and company financial performance (30% weight). The target bonus percentage varies by grade level (10-30% of annual CTC). You will receive a bonus letter with the detailed calculation before disbursement.
rejected: Bonuses are paid once a year. It depends on performance.

prompt: How can I save more tax from my salary?
chosen: Maximize tax savings by declaring investments during the April declaration window: Section 80C (up to ₹1.5 lakh via PF, PPF, ELSS, life insurance), Section 80D (health insurance premium up to ₹25,000), HRA exemption (submit rent receipts if applicable), NPS contribution under Section 80CCD(1B) (additional ₹50,000). Update your declarations on the HR portal under Tax > Investment Declaration. Submit proofs by February to avoid excess deduction in March.
rejected: You can save tax with some investments. Talk to a CA.

prompt: What is the difference between CTC and take-home salary?
chosen: CTC (Cost to Company) is your total annual compensation package including all components: Basic Pay, HRA, Special Allowance, employer PF contribution, insurance premium, gratuity, and variable pay. Take-home salary (net pay) is what you actually receive monthly after deductions: employee PF (12% of Basic), income tax (TDS), professional tax, and insurance premium. Typically, take-home is 60-70% of CTC depending on your tax slab and declarations.
rejected: CTC is the total cost and take-home is less because of deductions.

prompt: How do I prepare for my performance review?
chosen: Prepare for your performance review by: 1) Reviewing your goals set at the beginning of the cycle and documenting achievements with metrics, 2) Gathering evidence of impact (emails, project outcomes, client feedback), 3) Completing your self-assessment form on the Performance portal before the deadline, 4) Preparing examples for each competency area, 5) Listing development areas and your plan to address them, 6) Preparing questions about career growth and next-cycle goals for discussion with your manager.
rejected: Just fill out the self-assessment form before the meeting.

prompt: What should I do if I receive a poor performance rating?
chosen: If you receive a poor rating: 1) Ask your manager for specific examples and areas needing improvement, 2) Request a clear development plan with measurable milestones, 3) If you disagree, add your comments to the review form and consider filing a formal appeal within 10 working days, 4) Request more frequent check-ins (bi-weekly recommended) to track progress, 5) Leverage training resources and mentorship programs available through HR. A single poor rating does not mean career stagnation — demonstrating improvement in the next cycle is valued.
rejected: Bad ratings happen. Just work harder next time.

prompt: How does performance rating affect my increment?
chosen: Performance rating directly impacts your annual increment percentage. The typical correlation is: 'Exceptional' (top 10%) receives 12-15% increment, 'Exceeds Expectations' receives 9-12%, 'Meets Expectations' receives 5-8%, 'Needs Improvement' receives 0-3%, and 'Underperforms' receives no increment and may trigger a PIP. These ranges may vary based on department budget and market adjustments. The exact increment is communicated with your April salary revision letter.
rejected: Better rating means better increment. That's how it works.

prompt: Can I work from home permanently?
chosen: Permanent remote work arrangements are considered on a case-by-case basis and require VP-level approval. To apply, discuss with your manager first, then submit a Permanent WFH Request through the HR portal with business justification. Factors considered include: role suitability (client-facing roles may be excluded), performance history, team collaboration requirements, and data security needs. A formal remote work agreement with specific terms will be issued if approved.
rejected: It depends. Some people work from home permanently. Ask your manager.

prompt: What tools should I use for communication while working from home?
chosen: For WFH communication, use the company-approved tools: Microsoft Teams for instant messaging and video calls, Outlook for email correspondence, SharePoint/OneDrive for document collaboration, Jira/Asana for project tracking, and VPN for secure access to internal systems. Ensure your Teams status accurately reflects your availability. For sensitive discussions, use Teams calls rather than personal messaging apps. All work communication must remain on company-approved platforms for security and compliance.
rejected: Use Teams and email. That should be enough.

prompt: I lost a receipt for a business expense. What should I do?
chosen: If you've lost a receipt, you can still claim the expense with an alternative proof: credit/debit card statement showing the transaction, email confirmation of booking, or a signed self-declaration form (available on the expense portal) for amounts under $50. For amounts above $50 without any supporting document, manager approval via email is required along with the self-declaration. Include a note explaining the lost receipt when submitting the claim.
rejected: Without a receipt you might not get reimbursed. Try to find it.

prompt: Can I book a premium hotel for my business trip?
chosen: Hotel bookings must fall within your grade-level budget: Associate/Senior Associate: up to $150/night, Manager: up to $200/night, Senior Manager/Director: up to $300/night, VP and above: up to $450/night. Bookings exceeding these limits require pre-approval from your department head via the travel request form. All bookings must be made through the company travel portal for rate compliance and duty of care tracking.
rejected: Book whatever hotel you want as long as it's reasonable.

prompt: How do I add a family member to my health insurance?
chosen: Add family members during the annual enrollment window (November) or within 30 days of a qualifying life event (marriage, childbirth, adoption). Navigate to HR Portal > Benefits > Health Insurance > Add Dependent. Submit required documents: marriage certificate for spouse, birth certificate for children, or age proof for dependent parents. Changes take effect from the 1st of the following month. Mid-year additions outside qualifying events are not permitted.
rejected: Go to the HR portal and add them to your insurance.

prompt: Does my health insurance cover pre-existing conditions?
chosen: Yes, the company group health insurance covers pre-existing conditions from Day 1 of enrollment with no waiting period. This is a significant advantage over individual policies which typically have 2-4 year waiting periods. Coverage includes hospitalization, treatment, and medication for declared pre-existing conditions. However, you must declare all pre-existing conditions during enrollment for seamless claim processing.
rejected: I think insurance covers most things. Check the policy document.

prompt: What happens to my health insurance after I leave the company?
chosen: Your company health insurance coverage continues until the last day of the month in which your employment ends. After that, you have two options: 1) Port your group policy to an individual health insurance plan within 30 days of coverage ending (no fresh medical underwriting required), or 2) Purchase COBRA continuation coverage for up to 18 months at full premium cost. HR will provide detailed transition options during your exit process.
rejected: Insurance stops when you leave. You'll need to get your own.

prompt: I haven't received my laptop on my first day. What should I do?
chosen: If your laptop isn't ready on Day 1, contact the IT helpdesk immediately (ext. 3333 or it.helpdesk@company.com). They will provide a loaner device within 2 hours for immediate work access. Meanwhile, inform your manager and HR coordinator. The standard SLA for new hire device provisioning is Day 1, so any delay should be escalated. Your permanent device with full configuration will be delivered within 2 business days maximum.
rejected: Wait for IT to sort it out. These things happen sometimes.

prompt: What should I learn during my first 30 days?
chosen: During your first 30 days, focus on: 1) Complete all mandatory onboarding modules on the LMS (compliance, security, policies), 2) Understand your team's current projects and priorities, 3) Learn the tools and systems used by your team, 4) Meet key stakeholders identified by your manager, 5) Review your 30-60-90 day plan with your manager, 6) Set up recurring 1-on-1s with your manager and buddy, 7) Understand the team's coding standards/processes, 8) Complete your first small deliverable. Your buddy and manager are your primary resources.
rejected: Just follow what your manager tells you and learn as you go.

prompt: Can I negotiate a shorter notice period?
chosen: Early release from notice period can be requested but is at management's discretion. Submit a formal request to your manager with the reason (new employer's joining date, personal circumstances). If approved, the days not served may either be waived entirely or deducted from your final settlement as notice period shortfall (calculated at per-day Basic Pay rate). Approval likelihood increases if your knowledge transfer is complete and a successor is identified.
rejected: You can try asking but they might not agree.

prompt: What should I include in my resignation letter?
chosen: Your resignation letter should include: 1) Clear statement of resignation, 2) Your proposed last working day (based on notice period), 3) Brief reason for leaving (optional but professional), 4) Offer to assist with transition and knowledge transfer, 5) Gratitude for opportunities received. Keep it concise (3-4 paragraphs), professional in tone, and submit it to your manager and HR simultaneously via email with the subject 'Resignation - [Your Name] - [Employee ID]'. A follow-up formal letter may be requested by HR.
rejected: Just write that you're resigning and when your last day will be.

prompt: Will the company provide a relieving letter?
chosen: Yes, the company issues a relieving letter to all employees who complete their full notice period and exit clearance successfully. The letter is generated within 7 working days of your last working day and sent to your personal email. It confirms your employment dates, designation, and that you left on good terms. Additionally, you receive an experience certificate detailing your role and responsibilities. Contact HR if you haven't received these within 10 days.
rejected: Yes, you'll get a relieving letter when you leave.

prompt: Do I need to complete compliance training every year?
chosen: Yes, mandatory compliance training must be completed annually by all employees. The training modules cover: Anti-Bribery and Corruption, Data Privacy and Protection, Information Security Awareness, Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH), Insider Trading, and Code of Conduct refresher. Training assignments appear on your LMS dashboard in January with a 30-day completion deadline. Failure to complete by the deadline results in automated reminders, manager escalation, and potential system access restrictions.
rejected: Yes, there's some annual training you need to do.

prompt: What happens if I accidentally send confidential data to the wrong person?
chosen: Immediately report the incident to IT Security (security@company.com or ext. 2222) within 1 hour of discovery. Do not attempt to recall or delete the email yourself — the security team has proper tools for this. Provide details: what data was sent, to whom, when, and the sensitivity level. The Incident Response Team will assess the breach severity, attempt data recall, notify affected parties if required, and guide you on next steps. Honest, timely reporting is not penalized under the company's good-faith reporting policy.
rejected: Try to recall the email. If that doesn't work, tell IT.

prompt: Can I expense my work-from-home internet bill?
chosen: Yes, employees working from home receive a monthly WFH allowance of $50 that covers internet and utility costs. This is automatically added to your salary and does not require separate expense claims or receipts. If you need enhanced internet connectivity for specific work requirements (large file transfers, video production), you may request additional reimbursement up to $100/month with manager approval and IT confirmation of the business need.
rejected: The company might reimburse internet. Check the policy.

prompt: What should I do if I witness harassment in the workplace?
chosen: If you witness harassment: 1) Ensure the victim's immediate safety, 2) Document what you observed (date, time, location, parties involved, specific behaviors), 3) Report to the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) through the online portal, HR directly, or the anonymous ethics hotline, 4) Offer to provide a witness statement if asked. You are protected under the non-retaliation policy for reporting in good faith. Bystander intervention is encouraged when safe — a simple 'Is everything okay?' can help. Do not confront the alleged harasser directly.
rejected: Report it to HR if you think it's serious.

prompt: Am I allowed to work from a coffee shop?
chosen: Working from public spaces like coffee shops is permitted for short durations but requires security precautions: use VPN for all company network access, enable privacy screen filter on your laptop, avoid video calls discussing confidential matters, never leave devices unattended, and do not access highly confidential documents (financial, HR, legal) on public Wi-Fi even with VPN. For regular WFH days, a secure home environment is strongly preferred over public spaces.
rejected: Sure, you can work from anywhere as long as you're online.

prompt: How do I get access to the gym in the office building?
chosen: To access the office gym, submit a request through the Facilities portal under Wellness > Gym Access. You'll need to complete a health declaration form and sign the liability waiver. Access is activated on your employee ID card within 2 working days. Gym hours are 6:00 AM to 9:00 PM. A fitness orientation session is mandatory before first use. The company subsidizes the $50/month membership — only $25 is deducted from salary.
rejected: There's a gym in the building. Ask facilities about getting access.

prompt: Can I bring a guest to the office cafeteria?
chosen: Yes, guests are welcome in the cafeteria. Register them through the Visitor Management System as a 'cafeteria visitor' — this provides a temporary badge valid for the cafeteria area only (no office floor access). Guest meals are charged at full price (no company subsidy) and billed to the hosting employee's meal card or paid via cash/card. Pre-registration is required at least 2 hours before the visit.
rejected: I think you can bring guests. Just check at the reception.

prompt: How do I find out what training programs are available?
chosen: Browse available training programs through the Learning Management System (LMS) accessible via the HR portal. Training is categorized by: Technical Skills, Leadership Development, Soft Skills, Compliance (mandatory), and Industry Certifications. Filter by delivery mode (in-person, virtual, self-paced), duration, and skill level. Your personalized learning recommendations appear on the LMS dashboard based on your role, level, and IDP goals. New programs are announced in the monthly Learning Newsletter.
rejected: Check the training portal. There should be courses listed there.

prompt: Will the company sponsor my MBA degree?
chosen: The company may sponsor your MBA through the tuition reimbursement program, covering up to $10,000 per year for approved graduate programs. Eligibility requires: minimum 1 year of confirmed service, the program must be from an accredited institution, coursework must be relevant to your current or planned future role. Apply through the LMS with program details and manager endorsement. Upon approval, you must maintain a 3.0+ GPA and commit to 2 years post-completion employment or repay the amount.
rejected: They might pay for it. You'll have to ask HR.

prompt: I forgot my password. How do I reset it?
chosen: Reset your password through the Self-Service Password Reset portal (password.company.com) using your registered mobile number or backup email for OTP verification. If you're locked out of the reset portal, contact IT Helpdesk (ext. 3333, available 24/7) with your employee ID for identity verification and manual reset. New passwords must be 12+ characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character. Passwords expire every 90 days.
rejected: Contact IT helpdesk and they'll reset it.

prompt: Can I install software on my work laptop without approval?
chosen: No, all software installations require approval through the IT Service Portal, even free/open-source software. This is to ensure security compliance, license management, and system stability. Submit a request with software name, version, download source, and business justification. Pre-approved software (listed on the IT portal) is auto-installed within 24 hours. Non-standard software requires security review (3-5 days). Installing unapproved software is a policy violation and may trigger a security audit.
rejected: Better not. You should ask IT first.

prompt: My manager is treating me unfairly. What are my options?
chosen: If you believe you're being treated unfairly, you have several escalation paths: 1) Document specific instances with dates, witnesses, and impact, 2) Discuss directly with your manager if safe to do so, 3) Escalate to your skip-level manager for an independent perspective, 4) Contact your HR Business Partner for confidential guidance and potential mediation, 5) File a formal grievance through the Grievance Portal for investigation, 6) Use the anonymous ethics hotline if you fear retaliation. The company guarantees non-retaliation for good-faith reports.
rejected: Talk to HR about it. They should be able to help.

prompt: Can HR mediate a conflict between me and a colleague?
chosen: Yes, HR provides professional mediation services for workplace conflicts. To request mediation: raise a ticket with your HR Business Partner describing the conflict without naming parties initially. HR will assess the situation and propose mediation if appropriate. Both parties must agree to participate. A trained mediator facilitates a structured conversation to find mutually acceptable resolution. The process is confidential, non-punitive, and typically resolved within 2-3 sessions.
rejected: HR can help if you're having issues with a colleague.

prompt: How do I join an Employee Resource Group?
chosen: Browse available Employee Resource Groups (ERGs) on the D&I portal under Communities: Women's Network, LGBTQ+ Alliance, Veterans Group, Disability Network, Cultural Heritage groups, Working Parents, and Young Professionals. Click 'Join' on any group to become a member — no approval required. Each ERG hosts monthly meetings, events, and mentoring opportunities. You can join multiple ERGs. Leadership roles within ERGs are filled through annual elections and count toward your performance contributions.
rejected: Check the intranet for employee groups you can join.

prompt: What should I do if I experience discrimination at work?
chosen: If you experience discrimination based on gender, race, religion, age, disability, sexual orientation, or any protected characteristic: 1) Document the incidents (dates, context, witnesses, specific actions/words), 2) Report to the Internal Complaints Committee via the online portal, your HR Business Partner, or the anonymous ethics hotline, 3) The company will initiate a confidential investigation within 7 days, 4) You are fully protected under the non-retaliation policy. The D&I team also provides support resources including counseling. The company has zero tolerance for discrimination.
rejected: That's not okay. You should report it to HR.

prompt: Can I work during my notice period from home?
chosen: Working from home during notice period follows the same hybrid policy — up to 3 WFH days per week with manager approval. However, managers may require more office presence during notice for knowledge transfer and handover activities. Discuss and agree on a schedule with your manager. Complete WFH during notice period is only permitted in exceptional circumstances (medical reason with documentation) and requires HR approval.
rejected: Ask your manager if WFH is okay during notice.

prompt: I need to take time off for a family emergency. What do I do?
chosen: For immediate family emergencies, inform your manager as soon as possible by any available means (call, text, email). Apply for leave retroactively within 2 working days of returning. You can use: casual leave, earned leave, or emergency personal leave (up to 3 days for family crisis situations). For bereavement, 5 days paid leave is available for immediate family. If the emergency requires extended absence, discuss with HR about additional unpaid leave or work-from-home arrangements.
rejected: Just inform your manager and apply for leave when you can.

prompt: How do I claim my meal allowance?
chosen: Meal allowance for business-related meals (client meetings, late working, business travel) is claimed through the expense portal. For regular office meals, your monthly meal card handles the subsidy automatically. For business meal claims: upload the restaurant receipt, specify the business purpose and attendees, and submit within 15 days. Limits: client meals up to $50/person, late working meals up to $15, team meals require manager pre-approval for the total amount.
rejected: Submit the receipt on the expense portal and it should get reimbursed.

prompt: Is there a referral bonus for recommending candidates?
chosen: Yes, the employee referral program offers substantial bonuses: $1,000 for entry-level positions, $2,500 for mid-level/specialist roles, $5,000 for senior/leadership positions. The bonus is paid in two installments — 50% when the referred candidate joins and 50% after they complete 6 months. Submit referrals through the Referral Portal with the candidate's resume. There's no limit on referrals per employee. Referrals for direct reportee positions are excluded.
rejected: Yes, there's a referral bonus. The amount depends on the role.

prompt: What if I can't come to office on a mandatory office day?
chosen: If you cannot attend on a mandatory office day (typically Tuesday/Thursday), inform your manager before 9:00 AM with the reason. Occasional exceptions for genuine reasons (medical appointment, family emergency, home repair emergency) are typically approved. However, habitual absence from mandatory days without valid reason may result in: WFH privilege review, discussion with HR, and potential policy violation flagging. If traveling, plan schedules around mandatory days where possible.
rejected: Just let your manager know you won't be in.

prompt: Can I permanently relocate to another city and work remotely?
chosen: Permanent relocation to another city with full remote work requires a formal request process: 1) Submit a Permanent Remote Work Request through HR portal with business justification, 2) Manager assessment of role suitability, 3) VP-level approval, 4) Tax and compliance review by Legal/Finance (for cross-state implications), 5) If approved, a Remote Work Agreement is executed specifying terms. Factors considered include: time zone overlap with team, occasional office visit requirements, and tax jurisdiction implications.
rejected: That's usually not allowed unless you get special permission.

prompt: How do I set SMART goals for my performance review?
chosen: SMART goals framework for performance reviews: Specific (clearly define what you'll achieve), Measurable (quantify with metrics — revenue, delivery dates, quality scores), Achievable (realistic given resources and constraints), Relevant (aligned with team and organizational objectives), Time-bound (clear deadline or milestones). Example: 'Reduce customer support ticket resolution time from 48 hours to 24 hours by Q3 through implementing the new ticketing workflow.' Set 4-6 goals covering delivery, development, and collaboration dimensions.
rejected: SMART goals should be specific and measurable. Your manager can help you set them.

prompt: My colleague got promoted but I didn't. Why?
chosen: Promotions are determined by multiple factors: consistent performance ratings across 2+ cycles, demonstrated competency at the next level (not just excelling at current level), business need for the role, available budget, and manager recommendation through the promotion panel. Each case is individually assessed. Request a specific feedback conversation with your manager about: what was the gap, what's needed for next cycle, and what development plan can bridge it. HR can share general promotion criteria for your level.
rejected: Promotions depend on many factors. Focus on your own growth.

prompt: I injured myself at work. What should I do?
chosen: For a workplace injury: 1) Seek immediate first aid (first aid stations on every floor, trained responders available), 2) For serious injuries, call emergency services and inform Security (ext. 1111), 3) Report the incident to your manager and the Safety team within 24 hours via the Incident Reporting portal, 4) Visit the company-empaneled doctor for documentation even for minor injuries, 5) File a workers' compensation claim through HR if applicable. All medical expenses for workplace injuries are fully covered. Rest and recovery time is treated as paid duty leave.
rejected: Get medical help first, then report it to your manager.

prompt: Are there any health hazards in the office I should know about?
chosen: The Facilities team conducts regular environmental assessments. Common office hazards addressed include: ergonomic strain (mitigated through proper workstation setup — request an assessment), air quality (HVAC filters maintained quarterly, CO2 monitors on each floor), noise levels (quiet zones available, noise-canceling headphones recommended for open areas), screen fatigue (follow 20-20-20 rule: every 20 min, look 20 feet away for 20 seconds), and trip hazards (report immediately to Facilities).
rejected: The office is safe. Talk to facilities if you have concerns.

prompt: How do I get VPN access for remote work?
chosen: VPN access is provisioned automatically for all employees. To set up: 1) Download the company VPN client from the IT Self-Service portal (or it's pre-installed on company devices), 2) Log in with your employee credentials + MFA token, 3) Select the nearest server location for best performance. If you encounter issues, IT Helpdesk (ext. 3333) provides 24/7 support. VPN must be active whenever accessing company resources from outside the office. Split-tunneling is disabled for security.
rejected: IT should have given you VPN. Contact them if it's not working.

prompt: What should I do if I receive a suspicious email?
chosen: If you receive a suspicious email: 1) Do NOT click any links or download attachments, 2) Do NOT reply to the sender, 3) Forward the email as an attachment to phishing@company.com, 4) Report it using the 'Report Phishing' button in Outlook, 5) Delete the email from your inbox. Signs of phishing include: urgent language, unknown senders, misspelled domains, requests for credentials/money, and unexpected attachments. If you accidentally clicked a link, immediately disconnect from the network and call IT Security (ext. 2222).
rejected: Don't click anything and delete it. Report it to IT if you're worried.

prompt: Can I change my PF contribution percentage?
chosen: The statutory employee PF contribution is 12% of Basic Pay, which is mandatory. However, you can increase your voluntary PF contribution (VPF) up to 100% of Basic Pay for additional tax-free savings. To modify VPF: submit a request through the HR portal under Benefits > Provident Fund > Modify VPF by the 10th of any month for it to take effect from the following month. Reducing VPF is also possible with the same timeline. Employer contribution remains fixed at 12%.
rejected: PF is 12% mandatory. You might be able to increase it voluntarily.

prompt: Does the company offer any retirement planning assistance?
chosen: Yes, comprehensive retirement planning support includes: 1) Employee Provident Fund (12%+12% contribution), 2) National Pension Scheme option (additional 10% with tax benefits), 3) Gratuity (15 days/year after 5 years of service), 4) Free financial planning sessions with our partner advisory firm (2 sessions/year), 5) Retirement planning workshops for employees aged 45+, 6) Superannuation fund option for senior management, 7) Online retirement corpus calculator on the benefits portal.
rejected: There's PF and gratuity. That should cover retirement.

prompt: Can I use company email for personal communication?
chosen: Limited personal use of company email is permitted, provided it: does not interfere with work responsibilities, is not used for commercial/business purposes outside the company, does not contain offensive or inappropriate content, does not violate any company policies, and is not used for mass mailings. Be aware that company emails are subject to monitoring and archiving per the Information Security Policy. For sensitive personal matters, use personal email accounts on personal devices.
rejected: Try to keep it professional but occasional personal emails are fine.

prompt: What is the policy if the office has to close unexpectedly?
chosen: In case of unexpected office closure (power failure, natural disaster, security threat): 1) The Crisis Communication team sends alerts via SMS, email, and the company app within 30 minutes of the decision, 2) Employees should work from home for the duration of closure, 3) If WFH is not feasible, the day is treated as paid administrative leave, 4) Critical operations team members may be directed to alternate sites, 5) Office reopening is communicated through the same channels. Always ensure your emergency contact info and phone number are current.
rejected: If the office closes, you'll work from home or take the day off.

prompt: Am I covered if I have an accident during my commute?
chosen: Yes, the company's Group Personal Accident (GPA) insurance covers accidents during your daily commute between home and office. Coverage includes: accidental death (3x CTC), permanent disability (proportional to degree), and hospitalization for injuries. To claim, report the accident to HR within 48 hours with a police/medical report. The commute must be via the direct/regular route. Detours for personal errands may not be covered.
rejected: I think the company insurance covers commute accidents. Check your policy document.

prompt: How do I request a name change in company records?
chosen: To update your name in company records (due to marriage, legal name change): submit a request through HR Portal > My Profile > Name Change with supporting documents — gazette notification or court order for legal name change, marriage certificate for post-marriage name change. Update is processed within 5-7 working days across all systems (HR, payroll, IT, insurance). A new employee ID card is issued. Update your PAN, Aadhaar, and bank account separately with those institutions.
rejected: Contact HR with your new name documents and they'll update the system.

prompt: What is the company's approach to flexible work for new parents?
chosen: New parents receive enhanced flexibility through the Parental Transition Program: 1) Gradual return to work — 80% schedule for first 4 weeks at full pay after parental leave, 2) Priority for WFH days (up to 4 days/week for 3 months post-return), 3) Flexible start/end times, 4) Access to lactation rooms and nursing breaks (30 min twice daily for nursing mothers), 5) Emergency backup childcare (10 days/year), 6) Parental support group membership, 7) Reduced travel expectations for 6 months post-return.
rejected: New parents can request flexible hours. Talk to your manager.

prompt: How do I give feedback about company policies?
chosen: Multiple channels exist for policy feedback: 1) Quarterly pulse surveys include open-text questions on policies, 2) Town hall Q&A sessions with leadership (held monthly), 3) HR Office Hours (weekly drop-in sessions), 4) Policy feedback form on the HR portal (anonymous option available), 5) Employee representatives on the Policy Review Committee raise aggregated feedback, 6) Direct conversation with your HR Business Partner. All feedback is reviewed by the Policy team, and updates are communicated through policy revision announcements.
rejected: You can mention it in surveys or tell HR.

prompt: What happens if I fail the background verification?
chosen: If background verification reveals discrepancies: 1) HR contacts you within 48 hours to discuss the findings, 2) You are given 7 working days to provide clarification or corrected documentation, 3) Minor discrepancies (date variations, title differences) are typically resolved with explanation, 4) Major discrepancies (fabricated qualifications, undisclosed terminations, criminal record) may result in offer withdrawal for new hires or termination during probation for joined employees. The process follows principles of natural justice.
rejected: If verification fails, your offer might be withdrawn.

prompt: Can I request unpaid leave for personal projects?
chosen: Unpaid personal leave can be requested for up to 30 days per year. Submit through the Leave portal under 'Leave Without Pay' with dates and reason. Manager and HR approval required. During unpaid leave: health insurance continues (company contribution maintained), PF contributions are paused, the period does not count toward tenure for gratuity calculation, and your position is held. For longer personal projects (1-6 months), consider applying for a sabbatical if eligible (5+ years service).
rejected: You can ask for unpaid leave but it depends on your manager.

prompt: How do I know if I'm eligible for gratuity?
chosen: You become eligible for gratuity upon completing 5 continuous years of service with the company. Gratuity is calculated as: (Last drawn Basic + DA) × 15 × years of service / 26. The maximum statutory limit is ₹20 lakh (subject to government revisions). Gratuity is payable upon: resignation (after 5 years), retirement, death, or disability regardless of tenure. Your current gratuity projection is viewable on the HR portal under Benefits > Retirement > Gratuity Estimator.
rejected: Gratuity kicks in after 5 years of service. HR can tell you the exact amount.

prompt: What is the company's stance on employees forming unions?
chosen: The company respects employees' right to freedom of association as per applicable labor laws. While there is currently no employee union, the company maintains open communication channels (town halls, skip-level meetings, employee representatives, grievance mechanisms) to address concerns. The company believes in direct engagement and transparent dialogue. Employees who wish to organize are not penalized, consistent with legal protections and company values.
rejected: The company prefers direct communication rather than unions.

prompt: How is overtime calculated for night shift workers?
chosen: Night shift workers (10 PM - 6 AM) receive a 20% shift differential premium on their hourly rate. Overtime beyond the 8-hour shift is calculated at 1.5x the enhanced rate (base rate + 20% differential). For example, if base hourly is $25, night differential makes it $30/hour, and overtime would be $45/hour. Weekly overtime beyond 48 hours is paid at 2x rate. All night shift overtime must be pre-approved and logged in the attendance system.
rejected: Overtime is 1.5x your regular rate for extra hours worked.

prompt: What support is available if I'm relocating for the company?
chosen: Company-initiated relocations include comprehensive support: 1) Moving expenses up to $10,000 domestically (international: up to $25,000), 2) Temporary housing for 30 days, 3) House-hunting trip (3 days paid leave + travel), 4) School search assistance for children, 5) Spouse career support services (resume help, job placement assistance), 6) Settling-in allowance (1 month salary), 7) Cost of living adjustment if moving to a higher-cost city, 8) Cultural orientation for international moves, 9) Tax assistance for cross-jurisdiction implications.
rejected: The company provides some relocation benefits. HR will give you the details.

prompt: How do I provide suggestions for improving workplace culture?
chosen: Share workplace culture suggestions through: 1) The quarterly engagement survey's open-text section, 2) The Culture Champions program (apply to join this employee-led initiative), 3) Monthly 'Ideas Box' on the intranet (reviewed by the People & Culture team), 4) Direct discussion with your HR Business Partner, 5) Town hall open forum questions, 6) Team retrospectives where you can propose team-level improvements, 7) The internal social platform's #ideas-and-feedback channel. High-impact suggestions are recognized through the Innovation Award program.
rejected: You can share ideas in the surveys or with HR.

prompt: What happens if the company discovers I have a second job?
chosen: If undisclosed secondary employment is discovered, the following process applies: 1) HR schedules a discussion within 48 hours, 2) You're asked to provide a formal explanation and details of the outside work, 3) Assessment against conflict of interest criteria and policy compliance, 4) Possible outcomes range from: retroactive approval (if no conflict exists), requirement to cease the activity within 14 days, written warning, or termination in severe cases (competitive activity, performance impact, or using company resources). Proactive disclosure through the COI form avoids this process entirely.
rejected: You could get in trouble. It's better to disclose any side work.

prompt: How do I access the employee self-service portal?
chosen: Access the HR Self-Service Portal at hr.company.com using your employee credentials (same as email login) with multi-factor authentication. Available features: personal information management, leave application, payslip download, tax declarations, benefits enrollment, expense claims, training registration, IT requests, and policy documents. Mobile access is available through the HR app (iOS/Android) — download from the app store and log in with employee SSO. First-time setup requires OTP verification.
rejected: Log into the HR portal with your work credentials.

prompt: Can I get a letter for visa application purposes?
chosen: Yes, HR provides employment verification letters for visa applications within 3 working days. Request through HR Portal > Document Requests > Visa Support Letter. Specify the embassy/consulate requirements and destination country. The letter typically includes: employment confirmation, designation, tenure, annual compensation (in requested currency), approved leave dates, and guarantee of continued employment. Additional letters (sponsorship, financial guarantee) may require manager and finance signatures.
rejected: HR can give you a letter. Just ask them what they need.

prompt: What is the policy on employees dating within the same team?
chosen: Workplace relationships between members of the same team are not prohibited but must be disclosed to HR when they develop beyond casual dating. This is to manage potential conflicts of interest, perception of favoritism, and team dynamics. Upon disclosure, HR evaluates whether a reporting structure change is needed (mandatory if one party has supervisory authority over the other). Both parties maintain professionalism at work and acknowledge the relationship in a voluntary disclosure form.
rejected: It's allowed but you should let HR know about it.

prompt: How do I handle a situation where my manager asks me to do something unethical?
chosen: If your manager requests something you believe is unethical or violates company policy: 1) Clearly but respectfully express your concern and ask for clarification of the request, 2) Document the interaction (email, written notes with date/time), 3) If the concern persists, do NOT comply with the unethical request, 4) Report to any of these channels: your skip-level manager, HR Business Partner, the Ethics Committee (ethics@company.com), or the anonymous ethics hotline, 5) You are fully protected under the whistleblower and non-retaliation policies. Never fear consequences for refusing unethical directives.
rejected: You don't have to do anything unethical. Report it to someone above your manager.

prompt: Is there a way to check my total years of service for benefits eligibility?
chosen: Check your total years of service on the HR portal under My Profile > Employment Details. The 'Continuous Service Date' determines eligibility for tenure-based benefits: earned leave accrual rate (increases at 3 years), gratuity (eligible at 5 years), sabbatical (eligible at 5 years), long-service awards (5-year milestones), and senior-level benefits. If you have prior service with an acquired entity, check with HR whether it counts toward continuous service tenure.
rejected: Your joining date is on the portal. Calculate from there.

prompt: What is the company's approach to work-life balance?
chosen: The company promotes work-life balance through: hybrid work model (3 WFH days/week), flexible hours, core hours only 10 AM-4 PM, no-meeting Fridays after 3 PM, manager training on boundary-setting, mental health days (2/year no questions asked), wellness program with gym and counseling, discouragement of after-hours emails (delayed delivery recommended), comp-off for extended work periods, generous leave policy (36 days/year), and quarterly work-life balance pulse checks. Leaders are expected to model healthy boundaries.
rejected: The company supports work-life balance with flexible hours and WFH options.

prompt: How do I transition from full-time to part-time employment?
chosen: To transition to part-time, submit a Flexible Work Arrangement request through HR portal with: proposed schedule (minimum 20 hours/week), duration (temporary or permanent), business impact assessment, and how responsibilities will be managed. Manager and HR approval required. Part-time employees receive: prorated salary, prorated leave, health insurance (50% employer contribution), PF continuation, and access to learning platforms. The transition preserves your tenure and employment continuity.
rejected: Ask HR about going part-time. They'll tell you if it's possible for your role.

prompt: What should I do if I have a complaint about the food in the cafeteria?
chosen: Submit cafeteria feedback through: 1) The digital feedback terminals at cafeteria exits (rate meals daily), 2) The Facilities portal under Cafeteria > Feedback/Complaint, 3) Monthly cafeteria committee meetings (open to all employees), 4) Direct communication with the Facilities Manager. For food safety concerns (contamination, allergic reaction), report immediately to the cafeteria supervisor and Facilities emergency line. The catering vendor's contract includes quality SLAs and complaints are tracked with response within 24 hours.
rejected: Tell facilities if the food isn't good.

prompt: What is the grace period for late arrival to office?
chosen: There is a 15-minute grace period. Standard work start time is 9:00 AM with flexible start allowed up to 10:00 AM. Arrival after 10:15 AM (10:00 AM + 15 min grace) is marked as late. Three late arrivals in a calendar month result in half-day casual leave deduction. Consistent tardiness (5+ times per quarter) triggers a manager-HR discussion. Exceptions for documented emergencies or transport disruptions are approved by your manager.
rejected: You have 15 minutes grace period. Don't be late regularly.

prompt: How do I mark my attendance if I forgot to punch in?
chosen: If you forget to punch in/out, raise a regularized attendance request through the HR portal under Attendance > Missed Punch within 48 hours. Include the actual time you arrived/left, and your manager must approve the request. Maximum 3 missed punch corrections allowed per month. Exceeding this limit requires HR escalation and is treated as a policy violation. Set a phone reminder to avoid this situation.
rejected: Tell your manager or fix it in the attendance system.

prompt: Can I combine sick leave and earned leave for a longer absence?
chosen: Yes, you can combine different leave types. For example, if you need 15 days off, you can use: remaining sick leave + earned leave + casual leave (if applicable). Apply through the HR portal specifying the split. The system automatically deducts from leave balances in priority order: casual leave first (expires Dec 31), then sick leave, then earned leave. Manager approval is required for the combined leave request, especially if it exceeds 7 consecutive working days.
rejected: Yes, you can mix leaves if needed. Just apply on the portal.

prompt: Do I get leave encashment at year end?
chosen: Earned leave (EL) balance exceeding 45 days at year end is automatically encashed at Basic Pay rate and added to your December salary. Casual leave and sick leave are NOT encashable and lapse on December 31st. Leave encashment is not paid out at the time of resignation unless you have exhausted all active leave entitlements. The encashment formula is: (Excess EL days over 45) × (Monthly Basic / 30).
rejected: Extra leaves get encashed if you have too many.

prompt: What if I need to take a call during WFH but my home network is down?
chosen: If your home internet fails during WFH: 1) Immediately inform your manager via mobile phone or cellular data, 2) Attempt to resolve the issue (ISP support call, mobile hotspot), 3) If unresolved within 2 hours, either commute to the office or use a personal leave day for the remainder, 4) Document the disruption and update your attendance record. Chronic connectivity issues (3+ occurrences in 2 months) may result in WFH privilege review. Ensure your home setup is reliable before opting for WFH.
rejected: Use your phone hotspot if internet fails. Or come to office.

prompt: Can I work from home on a public holiday for overtime pay?
chosen: Working on public holidays requires prior manager approval and is subject to business need, not simply location. If approved to work on a holiday: non-exempt employees receive overtime at 2x the regular hourly rate plus comp-off, exempt employees receive comp-off only (no overtime pay). Working from home on a holiday does not automatically qualify for overtime — the work must be specifically requested/approved by management. Simply being available or working voluntarily does not count.
rejected: You might get overtime for working on holidays. Ask your manager first.

prompt: How do I document my achievements for the year?
chosen: Maintain a running achievement log throughout the year using: 1) A personal document (spreadsheet or Word) with monthly entries, 2) The Achievement Tracker on the Performance portal, 3) Email yourself a summary after completing significant milestones. For each achievement, include: project name, your specific contribution, measurable impact (revenue, cost savings, quality improvement), stakeholder feedback, and skills demonstrated. Review and update this log monthly and before each performance review cycle.
rejected: Just keep track of what you do throughout the year.

prompt: What if my manager doesn't agree with my self-assessment?
chosen: Disagreement between self-assessment and manager rating is normal. The process is: 1) Your manager discusses the rating with you during the review meeting, explaining specific examples for the rating, 2) You can add your comments directly in the review form before finalizing, 3) If the gap is significant (more than one rating level), request a calibration discussion with HR, 4) Submit a formal appeal within 10 working days if you believe the rating is unjustified, with documented evidence. The final decision rests with the calibration committee.
rejected: If they disagree, you can appeal or just accept the rating.

prompt: I noticed an error in my payslip. What do I do?
chosen: Report payslip errors to the Payroll team within 7 days of salary credit: 1) Raise a ticket on the HR portal under Payroll > Discrepancy, 2) Attach a screenshot of the payslip with the error highlighted, 3) Provide supporting documentation (e.g., approved leave showing it shouldn't be LOP), 4) Payroll team investigates and responds within 5 working days. If an overpayment is discovered, recovery may be spread across 2-3 months to minimize impact. Underpayments are corrected in the next payroll cycle with a arrears adjustment.
rejected: Contact payroll about any mistakes on your payslip.

prompt: Can I get my salary credited early this month?
chosen: Early salary credit is only permitted in exceptional circumstances: medical emergency, natural disaster, or documented financial hardship. Submit a formal request to HR and Finance with supporting evidence. If approved, salary can be credited up to 5 business days early. This is a one-time exception per calendar year and does not alter the standard salary credit cycle for future months. Regular salary will continue to be credited on the last working day of each month.
rejected: Normally no, salary is paid on the fixed date. Ask HR if it's an emergency.

prompt: What is the coverage limit for dental treatment under health insurance?
chosen: Dental coverage under the company health insurance includes: routine check-ups and cleaning (up to $200/year), fillings and extractions (up to $500/year), root canal treatment (up to $800/year), and emergency dental care (up to $300/visit). Orthodontic treatments (braces, aligners) are NOT covered. Cosmetic dental procedures are excluded. Treatment must be obtained from network dentists listed in the insurance portal for cashless claims. Out-of-network treatments are reimbursed at 80% of the eligible amount.
rejected: Dental is covered up to some limit. Check with your insurance provider.

prompt: Can I opt out of the company health insurance?
chosen: Yes, employees may opt out of company health insurance by submitting a written declaration confirming alternative coverage (spouse's policy, individual plan). The employer contribution portion is NOT converted to cash or added to salary. Opting out means you and your dependents have no coverage from the company plan. You can re-enroll during the annual benefits enrollment window (November). Opt-out must be renewed annually. The company strongly recommends against opting out unless you have equally comprehensive coverage.
rejected: You can opt out but you won't get any extra money for it.

prompt: What if I don't complete the mandatory training on time?
chosen: Failure to complete mandatory compliance training by the 30-day deadline results in: 1) Automated email reminders at day 25, 28, and 30, 2) Manager notification on day 31, 3) System access restrictions starting day 35 (VPN access suspended, non-critical systems locked), 4) Escalation to HR and skip-level manager, 5) Notation in performance record affecting eligibility for promotions and bonuses, 6) Repeated non-compliance may be treated as a code of conduct violation. Complete all mandatory training within the deadline to avoid consequences.
rejected: You'll get reminders and eventually your access might be blocked.

prompt: Does the company recognize external certifications?
chosen: Yes, the company recognizes and rewards relevant external certifications: AWS, Azure, GCP (cloud certifications), PMP, Scrum Master, Six Sigma (project management), CISSP, CISM (security), SHRM, PHR (HR), CPA (finance). Rewards include: exam fee reimbursement, certification bonus ($500-$2,000 depending on certification level), recognition in monthly newsletter, and consideration in promotion decisions. The certification must be relevant to your current role or a role you're preparing for. Apply through the Learning portal with proof of certification.
rejected: Some certifications are recognized. HR has a list of approved ones.

prompt: I received an expensive gift from a vendor. What should I do?
chosen: For gifts valued above $50 from vendors, clients, or business partners: 1) Do NOT accept the gift immediately, 2) Politely explain the company policy, 3) If it has already been delivered, do not use it personally, 4) Report it to your manager and the Compliance team within 48 hours, 5) The gift will be logged in the Gift Registry and either: returned to the sender, donated to charity, or retained for office use (e.g., client meeting room). Cash gifts are NEVER acceptable under any circumstances. Violations may result in disciplinary action.
rejected: Report expensive gifts to Compliance and don't keep them.

prompt: What is the policy on insider trading?
chosen: Insider trading is strictly prohibited under company policy and securities laws. You must not: buy, sell, or trade company stock while in possession of material non-public information (MNPI), share MNPI with anyone outside the company, trade in client/partner securities based on MNPI, or attempt to benefit from information learned during employment. Trading blackout periods apply 2 weeks before earnings announcements and until 48 hours after public disclosure. Violations result in immediate termination and referral to regulatory authorities for criminal prosecution.
rejected: Don't trade on confidential information. It's illegal and you'll get fired.

prompt: Where is the assembly point in case of fire?
chosen: The primary assembly point is in the main parking area near the flagpole (visible from all building exits). Secondary assembly points are: North parking lot (for employees on floors 1-3), South parking lot (for floors 4-6). Evacuation maps are posted on every floor near elevators and stairwells — familiarize yourself with the nearest exit route. During fire drills or actual emergencies, proceed calmly to the nearest exit, do NOT use elevators, and report to your floor marshal for headcount. Do not leave the assembly area until the all-clear is given.
rejected: The assembly point is in the parking area. Follow the signs during evacuation.

prompt: How do I report a slippery floor or tripping hazard?
chosen: Report facility hazards immediately: 1) For immediate dangers (spills, exposed wires), alert people nearby and place a warning sign if available, 2) Call Facilities Helpdesk (ext. 4444) or submit through the Facilities portal, 3) For after-hours emergencies, contact Security (ext. 1111), 4) Include location details (floor, wing, nearest room number), 5) Take a photo if safe to do so. Facilities SLA: urgent hazards resolved within 2 hours, standard within 24 hours. You can track the ticket status on the portal.
rejected: Tell facilities about the hazard and they'll fix it.

prompt: How long does a grievance investigation take?
chosen: Standard grievance investigations are completed within 15-30 calendar days depending on complexity: simple grievances (policy clarification, minor disputes) are resolved within 15 days, complex cases (harassment, discrimination, financial disputes) may take up to 30 days with an interim update at day 15. The process includes: intake and acknowledgment (48 hours), fact-finding and interviews (7-14 days), deliberation and decision (5 days), communication of outcome (2 days). You can request status updates from your HR Business Partner at any time.
rejected: Investigations take a few weeks usually. HR will keep you updated.

prompt: Can I withdraw a grievance I filed?
chosen: Yes, you can withdraw a grievance at any point before the final decision by submitting a written withdrawal request to HR. However, if the grievance involves serious allegations (harassment, fraud, safety violations, discrimination), HR may continue the investigation even after withdrawal to ensure workplace safety and legal compliance. Withdrawing a grievance does not prevent you from filing a new grievance if similar issues arise in the future. Consult with HR before making a withdrawal decision.
rejected: You can withdraw it, but serious cases might still be investigated.

prompt: What happens during the probation review?
chosen: Probation reviews are conducted at 2-month, 4-month, and 6-month marks. Each review assesses: technical competency in role, learning pace, team collaboration, attendance and punctuality, adherence to company policies, and alignment with company values. The review process includes: self-assessment, manager evaluation meeting, documented feedback, and a pass/fail/extend decision. Successful completion results in formal confirmation email with full benefits activation. If extended, a specific improvement plan with timelines is provided. Failure leads to separation with 15 days notice.
rejected: Your manager reviews your performance at the end of probation.

prompt: Can I change teams during my first year?
chosen: Team changes within the first 12 months are generally discouraged as the focus should be on learning and contributing to your current team. However, exceptions are considered for: compelling business reasons (project realignment, organizational restructuring), significant skill mismatch with the role, or irreconcilable team dynamics (escalated to HR). To request a transfer: complete minimum 6 months in current role, obtain current manager's acknowledgment, demonstrate readiness for the target role, and apply through the Internal Job Portal. HR mediates the transition.
rejected: It's difficult to change teams early. Wait at least a year.

prompt: Do I get bonus payout if I resign before the payout date?
chosen: Bonus eligibility upon resignation depends on timing and tenure: if you resign before the bonus payout date (typically April) but have completed the full performance year (April-March), you receive a pro-rated bonus based on months worked during the year, paid within 45 days of your last working day. If you leave before completing the performance year, no bonus is payable. Employees who resign during the notice period on or before the payout date may forfeit the bonus at management discretion. Check your employment contract for specific terms.
rejected: You might get a partial bonus depending on when you leave. Ask HR.

prompt: What is the handover process when I resign?
chosen: The handover process begins on the day your resignation is accepted: 1) Create a comprehensive handover document covering: ongoing projects with status, key contacts, access credentials, pending deliverables, and process documentation, 2) Identify your successor or interim owner for each responsibility, 3) Schedule knowledge transfer sessions with the team (recorded for reference), 4) Complete all pending expense claims and return company assets, 5) Manager reviews and signs off on the handover checklist, 6) Exit clearance from IT, Finance, Admin, and HR. The handover must be complete before the relieving letter is issued.
rejected: Document your work and hand it over to whoever takes your place.

prompt: Can I store personal files on my work laptop?
chosen: Limited personal file storage is permitted on company devices: up to 5 GB for personal documents, photos, or media files. However: personal files are subject to company monitoring and data retention policies, sensitive personal data (financial records, health information) should NOT be stored on company devices, company IT can access, move, or delete personal files if needed for business purposes, and personal files are wiped when you leave the company or return your device. Use company-approved cloud storage (OneDrive personal folder) rather than local storage.
rejected: A small amount of personal files is okay. Don't store anything sensitive.

prompt: What should I do if my laptop is running slow?
chosen: For slow laptop performance: 1) Restart your device (solves 60% of issues), 2) Close unnecessary applications and browser tabs, 3) Check for pending Windows/software updates and install them, 4) Run a quick antivirus scan via the company security software, 5) Clear temporary files (Disk Cleanup tool), 6) If the issue persists, submit a ticket to IT Helpdesk (ext. 3333) with details of the problem, error messages, and when it started. For devices older than 3 years, request a hardware assessment — you may be eligible for a refresh.
rejected: Restart it and contact IT if the problem continues.

prompt: How can I volunteer for company events?
chosen: Volunteer for company events through: 1) The Events Committee open call (sent via email before major events), 2) Self-nomination on the Events portal under Get Involved, 3) Direct email to the events@company.com team, 4) Participation in the Town Hall planning committee (quarterly openings), 5) Joining specific event task forces (Annual Day, Sports Day, Charity Drive, Family Day). Volunteers receive recognition points redeemable for rewards, and volunteering hours count toward your community service contribution. Event roles include: logistics, content creation, emceeing, photography, and coordination.
rejected: Sign up for event volunteering through the events team or HR.

prompt: What is the company's policy on employee recognition?
chosen: The recognition program operates at multiple levels: spot recognition (peer-to-peer e-cards via the Recognition portal), monthly awards ($100-$250 gift cards for outstanding contribution), quarterly awards ($500 for excellence in company values categories), annual awards (Employee of the Year: $5,000 bonus + trophy), and milestone recognition (work anniversaries, project completions). Nominations can come from peers, managers, or clients. The Recognition Committee reviews and approves awards monthly. All recognitions are published in the monthly newsletter and count toward your performance record.
rejected: The company has various recognition programs. Check the portal.

prompt: Does the company accommodate religious observances?
chosen: Yes, the company accommodates religious observances through: 1) Floating holidays (2 per year) for festivals not on the standard holiday list, 2) Flexible scheduling on religious observance days (early departure, late arrival, or WFH), 3) Prayer/meditation rooms available on each campus, 4) Dietary accommodations in cafeteria (kosher, halal, vegetarian, vegan options daily), 5) Flexible dress code for religious attire, 6) Time off for religious ceremonies (approved as earned leave if floating holidays exhausted). Request accommodations through your manager or HR at least 5 days in advance.
rejected: Yes, you can take leave for religious occasions. Talk to your manager.

prompt: How do I request an accommodation for a disability?
chosen: Request workplace accommodations through HR: 1) Schedule a confidential meeting with your HR Business Partner, 2) Provide medical documentation from a licensed professional describing the limitation and recommended accommodations, 3) HR conducts an interactive assessment to identify reasonable accommodations (ergonomic equipment, modified schedule, assistive technology, workspace relocation), 4) Accommodations are implemented within 15 working days, 5) A 30-day follow-up ensures effectiveness. All information is kept strictly confidential. Undue hardship (significant cost or operational disruption) may limit certain accommodations.
rejected: Contact HR with a doctor's note about what you need.

prompt: Can I bring food to my desk?
chosen: Eating at your desk is permitted with the following guidelines: avoid strong-smelling or messy foods that may disturb colleagues, use a covered container and clean your workspace immediately after, dispose of food waste in designated bins (not regular trash), do not eat during meetings (unless it's a working lunch provided), and be mindful of allergens in shared spaces. Hot meals should be consumed in the cafeteria or designated break areas. Beverages (coffee, tea, water) are acceptable at all times at your desk.
rejected: Yes, but be considerate of others and clean up after yourself.

prompt: What is the policy on office decorations for festivals?
chosen: Festival decorations in common areas require Facilities approval and must follow these guidelines: decorations are permitted 3 days before and 2 days after the festival, no damage to walls/furniture (use removable tape, not nails or permanent adhesives), decorations must be inclusive and respectful of all cultures, no fire hazards (candles, open flames prohibited), common areas are first-come-first-served (submit a booking through Facilities), and the decorating team is responsible for cleanup. Desk-level personal decorations must be minimal and not obstruct walkways or safety equipment.
rejected: You can decorate with approval from Facilities. Just don't damage anything.

prompt: How do I book the auditorium for a team event?
chosen: Book the auditorium through the Facilities portal under Meeting Room Reservations: 1) Select Auditorium from the venue list, 2) Specify date, time (minimum 2 hours, maximum 8 hours), and expected attendance, 3) State the purpose and any special requirements (AV equipment, catering, stage setup), 4) Approval from Facilities Manager is required (2-3 business days), 5) For events with external guests, submit guest list to Security 24 hours in advance, 6) A Facilities staff member will coordinate setup. Booking is confirmed via email. Cancellations must be made 48 hours in advance.
rejected: Book it through the Facilities portal. They'll confirm availability.

prompt: What should I do if I'm locked out of the office building?
chosen: If locked out: 1) Contact Security at the main gate (ext. 1111) with your employee ID, 2) For early arrivals (before security desk opens at 7:00 AM), call the Facilities emergency number (posted on the main door), 3) If you lost your ID card, use the visitor entrance and present alternate photo ID to Security, who will issue a temporary pass, 4) For after-hours lockouts, Security maintains an access log and can manually verify your identity. Report lost ID cards immediately to prevent unauthorized access. Replacement ID cards take 3-5 days and cost $10.
rejected: Call security and they'll let you in.

prompt: How do I provide a reference for a former colleague?
chosen: If approached to provide a professional reference for a former colleague: 1) Ensure your information is factual and based on direct working experience, 2) Avoid sharing confidential company information or specific project details, 3) Focus on professional competencies, work ethic, and interpersonal skills, 4) Do not provide salary information, performance ratings, or reasons for leaving (these are verified through HR), 5) If the request is for a formal reference check, direct them to HR for employment verification, 6) Personal references are your discretion; avoid representing the company unless authorized.
rejected: You can give a reference based on your experience working with them.

prompt: What is the dress code for client meetings?
chosen: Client meetings require business formal attire regardless of the office dress code: men — collared shirt, formal trousers, tie optional, formal shoes (no sneakers), women — formal blouse with trousers/skirt, formal dress, or business suit (modest neckline, knee-length or longer), colors should be professional (navy, black, grey, white). For video calls, business casual is acceptable (collared shirt or blouse, no need for formal bottoms visible). When in doubt, it's better to be slightly overdressed than underdressed. Check with your manager if the client has specific expectations.
rejected: Wear formal clothes for client meetings. Better to be overdressed than casual.

prompt: Can I use my earned leave for a sabbatical?
chosen: Earned leave and sabbatical are different leave types. Earned leave is up to 45 days annually (with carry-forward limit), while a sabbatical is an extended unpaid leave of 1-6 months available after 5+ years of continuous service. You cannot combine earned leave with sabbatical to extend the period — they are separate applications. If approved for sabbatical, your earned leave balance remains intact and continues to accrue. You may use earned leave before or after the sabbatical period with separate manager approval.
rejected: Sabbatical and earned leave are different. They don't combine.

prompt: What is the policy on overtime approval?
chosen: All overtime must be pre-approved by your manager BEFORE working extra hours. Submit an overtime request through the Attendance portal specifying: date, estimated hours, business justification, and expected deliverable. Manager approval is required within 24 hours of submission. Unauthorized overtime (worked without approval) will not be compensated and may result in a discussion about time management. Emergency overtime (requested on the same day) requires manager verbal approval followed by portal documentation within 24 hours.
rejected: Get your manager's approval before working overtime.

prompt: How do I check my remaining leave balance?
chosen: Check your leave balance through: 1) HR Portal > Leave Management > Leave Balance (shows real-time balance for all leave types), 2) The HR mobile app (available on iOS/Android), 3) Monthly payslip (shows opening balance, utilized, and closing balance), 4) The self-service kiosk in the HR lobby. Balance updates in real-time when leave is approved or cancelled. For discrepancies, raise a ticket with HR within 7 days.
rejected: Check your leave balance on the HR portal or app.

prompt: What happens if I work on a national holiday?
chosen: Working on a national holiday (as listed in the official holiday calendar) requires business-critical justification and manager approval. If approved: non-exempt employees receive overtime pay at 3x the regular hourly rate PLUS a compensatory off day within 30 days, exempt employees receive comp-off only. All work on national holidays must be logged in the attendance system. The company generally discourages working on national holidays unless absolutely necessary for business continuity or client commitments.
rejected: You'll get overtime pay and a comp-off for working on holidays.

prompt: Can I take leave in the middle of a project deadline?
chosen: Leave during critical project phases or deadlines requires manager assessment of business impact. While employees have the right to planned leave, managers may: 1) Approve as requested if coverage is available, 2) Request postponement with alternative dates, 3) Approve with conditions (availability for urgent calls, advance completion of deliverables, knowledge transfer). If leave is denied during a critical period, discuss with HR about resource planning. Unplanned leave (sick, emergency) is handled differently — always approved with proper documentation.
rejected: Leave during deadlines depends on your manager's approval.

prompt: Does the company offer any fitness benefits?
chosen: Yes, fitness and wellness benefits include: subsidized gym membership ($25/month vs. $50 market rate), on-site gym with cardio and strength equipment, fitness orientation with a certified trainer (free), quarterly wellness challenges with prizes (steps, yoga, meditation), reimbursement for fitness-related purchases (yoga mat, running shoes up to $100/year), fitness webinars and workshops, standing desk option for all employees, and mental health days (2/year).
rejected: There's a gym in the office and some fitness benefits. Check the wellness program.

prompt: How do I report a pay discrepancy?
chosen: Report pay discrepancies immediately to the Payroll team: 1) Navigate to HR Portal > Payroll > Raise Query, 2) Select the issue type (incorrect salary, missing bonus, wrong tax deduction, LOP error, missing reimbursement), 3) Provide detailed explanation with supporting documents (approval emails, payslip screenshot), 4) Payroll investigates and responds within 5 working days, 5) If an error is confirmed, correction is made in the next payroll cycle with arrears. For urgent issues, email payroll@company.com directly or call ext. 5555.
rejected: Contact payroll with your payslip showing the issue.

prompt: What is the policy on employees sharing salary information?
chosen: The company does NOT prohibit employees from discussing their salaries with each other. Salary transparency is considered a right and discussing compensation does not violate any policy. However, employees are encouraged to approach HR or their manager directly if they have concerns about pay equity rather than making assumptions based on incomplete information. The annual pay equity audit ensures fair compensation across all demographics.
rejected: You can discuss salary, but it's better to talk to HR about pay concerns.

prompt: Can I get a company loan for personal reasons?
chosen: The company offers personal loans for specific purposes: home purchase (up to 50x monthly salary at 4% below market rate), vehicle purchase (up to 15x monthly salary), education (up to 10x monthly salary), medical emergencies (up to 5x monthly salary). Eligibility requires: minimum 3 years of continuous service, confirmed employment status, no outstanding loans or defaults, and satisfactory credit history. Apply through HR Portal > Benefits > Employee Loan with purpose, amount, and repayment plan. Approval takes 10-15 working days. Repayment is through monthly salary deduction over 36-60 months.
rejected: The company provides loans for specific needs. Ask HR about eligibility.

prompt: What should I do if my manager is unreachable during my leave?
chosen: If your manager is unreachable during an urgent leave-related matter: 1) Contact your skip-level manager or team lead for immediate guidance, 2) For leave extension requests, email HR with the reason and requested dates — HR can provisionally approve pending manager confirmation, 3) For emergencies affecting your leave (family crisis, health issue), contact HR directly who can provide support and flexibility, 4) Document all communication attempts. The company understands that emergencies require flexibility and will not penalize you for manager unavailability.
rejected: Try contacting your manager's manager or HR if you can't reach them.

prompt: How does the company handle public transportation strikes?
