chosen: During public transportation strikes, the company activates contingency measures: 1) Mandatory work-from-home for all employees who can work remotely, 2) For essential on-site roles: company-arranged alternative transport (buses, carpooling through the internal platform), 3) Flexible hours to accommodate alternative commute arrangements, 4) If neither WFH nor commute is feasible, the day is treated as paid administrative leave, 5) Communication is sent via email/SMS by 7:00 AM with instructions. Update your emergency contact and transportation preferences in the HR portal.
rejected: If there's a strike, you'll probably work from home or get the day off.

prompt: What is the company's policy on nepotism?
chosen: The company has a strict nepotism policy: relatives (spouse, siblings, parents, children, in-laws) cannot work in the same department, cannot have a direct/indirect reporting relationship, and cannot be involved in each other's hiring, performance review, or promotion decisions. Existing employees must declare any familial relationship with candidates or colleagues through the Conflict of Interest form. Violations may result in: reassignment to different teams, transfer of one party, or in severe cases, termination. Hiring relatives in different departments is permitted with full disclosure and HR approval.
rejected: Relatives can't work in the same team or report to each other.

prompt: Can I appeal a performance rating after it's finalized?
chosen: Yes, you can appeal a finalized performance rating within 15 working days of receiving it. The appeal process: 1) Submit a formal Performance Appeal to HR with specific grounds (procedural error, bias, new evidence not considered), 2) Include documented evidence: project outcomes, client emails, performance metrics, and comparative analysis, 3) HR assigns an independent review panel (skip-level manager + HR + cross-functional leader), 4) Panel reviews your case within 15 working days, 5) Decision is communicated in writing. The panel's decision is final. Appeals that proceed without merit do not carry negative consequences.
rejected: You can appeal within 15 days with evidence. HR will review it.

prompt: What is the policy on using personal email for work?
chosen: Personal email accounts must NOT be used for company business. All work-related communication must go through your official company email account. Exceptions are extremely limited: temporary use during IT system outages (with IT authorization), personal email for account recovery when company email is inaccessible. Sending confidential company data, customer information, or internal communications to personal email is a security violation and may result in disciplinary action. Use company-approved collaboration tools (Teams, SharePoint) for work communication, not personal email.
rejected: Don't use personal email for work. Use your company email account.

prompt: How do I get my experience certificate after leaving?
chosen: Your experience certificate is issued automatically as part of the exit process: 1) It is generated within 7 working days of your last working day, 2) Sent to your personal email address on file, 3) Includes: employment dates, designation, department, and a brief role description, 4) A physical copy is also mailed to your registered address if requested during exit clearance, 5) If you haven't received it within 10 days, contact HR at hr@company.com with your employee ID. The certificate is on company letterhead with an authorized signature and can be used for future employment verification.
rejected: HR sends it to your email after you leave. Contact them if you don't receive it.

prompt: What happens if I'm absent on the day of an important audit?
chosen: Absence during critical events (audits, major releases, client presentations) requires advance communication and contingency planning: 1) Inform your manager at least 24 hours in advance if possible, 2) Ensure your responsibilities are covered by a designated team member, 3) Provide handover notes and be available for urgent queries (if on sick leave, availability is optional based on health), 4) For unplanned absences (emergency, sudden illness), notify your manager immediately and arrange remote participation if feasible. Repeated absence during critical events may trigger a performance discussion.
rejected: Let your manager know and make sure someone covers your work.

prompt: Does the company support employees pursuing PhDs?
chosen: The company supports PhD pursuits through: 1) Tuition reimbursement up to $10,000/year for job-related research, 2) Flexible scheduling for coursework and research (requires manager and HR approval), 3) Access to company data and resources for research (subject to confidentiality agreement), 4) Reduced workload arrangements during critical research phases (up to 80% schedule for up to 6 months/year), 5) Academic sabbatical option (up to 3 months unpaid leave) for dissertation writing, 6) Company-sponsored research publications (with IP review). The PhD topic must align with company business or your professional development path.
rejected: The company may support PhD studies. Check with HR about available options.

prompt: Can I switch from night shift to day shift?
chosen: Shift changes are based on business needs and role requirements. To request a shift change: 1) Discuss with your manager about upcoming shift rotation cycles, 2) Submit a formal shift change request through HR portal with reason (health, family commitments, performance optimization), 3) Medical documentation strengthens health-related requests, 4) Shift changes are typically processed during quarterly rotation planning (advance notice of 4-6 weeks), 5) Temporary shift changes (up to 3 months) are more readily approved than permanent changes. Seniority and past shift coverage may be considered.
rejected: You can request a shift change but it depends on business needs.

prompt: What is the company's policy on workplace romances?
chosen: Workplace romances are not prohibited but must be disclosed to HR once the relationship is established, especially if there is a supervisory relationship. Upon disclosure: 1) HR assesses potential conflicts of interest (reporting structure, performance evaluation influence, compensation decisions), 2) If a conflict exists, one party is reassigned to a different team or reporting line, 3) Both parties sign a voluntary disclosure form acknowledging professional conduct expectations, 4) The company ensures no retaliation or favoritism. Undisclosed relationships where a conflict exists may result in disciplinary action.
rejected: It's allowed but you need to tell HR so they can manage any conflicts.

prompt: How do I request a change in my health insurance plan?
chosen: Health insurance plan changes are permitted only during the annual open enrollment period (typically November for the following calendar year). During enrollment: 1) Review plan options on the Benefits portal, 2) Compare coverage tiers (individual, family, family + parents), 3) Add or remove dependents with supporting documents, 4) Changes take effect January 1st. Mid-year changes outside open enrollment are only permitted with a qualifying life event (marriage, childbirth, adoption, divorce, death of a dependent) within 30 days of the event.
rejected: You can change your insurance plan during the annual enrollment period in November.

prompt: What is the policy on social media posting about work?
chosen: Social media posting about work must follow these guidelines: 1) Do not share confidential information, unreleased product details, financial data, or internal strategies, 2) Clearly state that opinions are personal and do not represent the company (add disclaimer to your profile), 3) Do not use the company logo as your profile picture without authorization, 4) Obtain consent before posting photos of colleagues or the workplace, 5) Do not engage with negative comments about the company publicly — escalate to Corporate Communications, 6) Violations may result in disciplinary action. Positive, professional sharing about company culture is generally encouraged.
rejected: Be careful about what you post. Don't share confidential information.

prompt: Can I get reimbursed for professional association memberships?
chosen: Yes, the company reimburses professional association memberships that are directly relevant to your role: IEEE, ACM, SHRM, PMI, ISACA, local bar associations, industry-specific bodies. Reimbursement covers: annual membership fees (up to $500/year), conference attendance associated with the membership, and access to professional development resources. Apply through HR Portal > Benefits > Professional Development with: membership details, cost, and relevance to your role. Manager approval required. Memberships must be maintained in good standing to qualify for reimbursement.
rejected: Yes, relevant professional memberships can be reimbursed. Ask HR.

prompt: What is the company's policy on drug and alcohol use?
chosen: The company maintains a zero-tolerance drug and alcohol policy: 1) Being under the influence of alcohol or illegal drugs while at work is strictly prohibited, 2) Alcohol is not permitted on company premises except at authorized events (holiday parties, client events with prior approval), 3) Prescription medications that may impair judgment must be disclosed to HR confidentially, and modified duties may be assigned, 4) Random drug testing may be conducted for safety-sensitive roles, 5) Employees reporting to work under the influence are sent home immediately (treated as unpaid leave) and face disciplinary action up to termination, 6) Support is available through the EAP for substance abuse issues.
rejected: No drugs or alcohol at work. It's a strict policy.

prompt: How does the company handle natural disaster leave?
chosen: For employees affected by natural disasters (floods, earthquakes, hurricanes, fires): 1) Emergency leave of up to 10 working days (paid) is provided for personal and family safety, home restoration, and dealing with authorities, 2) The company activates the Employee Relief Fund (up to $2,000 one-time assistance for severe losses), 3) Flexible work arrangements are provided (WFH, reduced hours, or temporary relocation), 4) If the employee's home is uninhabitable, the company assists with temporary housing, 5) Additional unpaid leave (up to 30 days) is available for recovery. Inform your manager and HR as soon as it's safe to do so.
rejected: The company provides emergency leave and financial assistance for natural disasters.

prompt: What is the company's policy on political activities at work?
chosen: Political activities at work are restricted: 1) No campaigning, soliciting, or distributing political materials on company premises or during work hours, 2) No use of company resources (email, printers, meeting rooms) for political purposes, 3) No wearing political campaign materials or clothing with explicit political messaging, 4) Personal political discussions with colleagues during breaks are permitted but must remain respectful, 5) The company does not endorse or financially support any political candidate or party, 6) Political activities on personal time outside work are your right and not subject to company policy.
rejected: No political campaigning at work. Personal political activities are your own business.

prompt: Can I get a copy of my employment contract?
chosen: Yes, you can request a copy of your employment contract at any time: 1) Access the signed digital copy through HR Portal > My Documents > Employment Contract, 2) For a certified hard copy, submit a request through HR Portal > Document Requests > Employment Contract Copy, 3) The document is provided within 3 working days, 4) For former employees, HR can provide copies upon identity verification (processing time: 7-10 days). Keep your contract in a secure location as it contains your terms of employment, compensation, and obligations.
rejected: Yes, you can get a copy from HR or the portal.

prompt: What is the policy on bringing pets to the office?
chosen: Pets are generally not permitted in the workplace except for: 1) Certified service animals (guide dogs, therapy dogs) with proper documentation — contact HR for accommodation, 2) Monthly 'Bring Your Pet to Work Day' (typically the last Friday, pets must be leashed, vaccinated, and well-behaved), 3) Occasional company-sanctioned pet events in outdoor common areas. Pets are not allowed in meeting rooms, cafeteria, or on production floors. Pet owners are responsible for any damage or disruption caused by their pets.
rejected: Pets aren't allowed except for service animals and special pet days.

prompt: How do I update my emergency contact details?
chosen: Update emergency contacts through: 1) HR Portal > My Profile > Emergency Contacts, 2) Add up to 3 emergency contacts with: full name, relationship, primary phone, alternate phone, and address, 3) At least one contact must be local (within 50 km of your work location), 4) Changes are saved immediately, 5) Review and update contacts annually during benefits enrollment or whenever your circumstances change. Emergency contacts are used for: medical emergencies, natural disasters, office evacuations, and critical incidents. Ensure your contacts are aware they are listed.
rejected: Update your emergency contacts on the HR portal.

prompt: What is the company's policy on whistleblowing?
chosen: The whistleblower policy protects employees who report illegal activities, fraud, corruption, safety violations, or serious policy breaches in good faith. Reporting channels: anonymous ethics hotline (available 24/7), ethics@company.com, direct report to HR or senior leadership, online whistleblower portal. Protections include: guaranteed anonymity (if requested), non-retaliation commitment, independent investigation by the Ethics Committee, regular status updates, legal support if needed, and disciplinary action against anyone who retaliates. Retaliation against whistleblowers is treated as a terminable offense.
rejected: Report wrongdoing through the ethics hotline. You'll be protected from retaliation.

prompt: Can I transfer my remaining leaves when I move to a different department?
chosen: Yes, when transferring internally to another department, your entire leave balance (casual, sick, and earned leave) transfers with you. Leave entitlements remain unchanged unless the new role has a different leave policy (e.g., international assignment). The transfer date serves as the transition point — leave applied before the transfer date is deducted from your balance in the old department, and leave after is managed by the new department. Coordinate with both managers to ensure accurate leave records during the transition.
rejected: Your leave balance moves with you when you transfer departments.

prompt: What is the policy on employees working for competitors after leaving?
chosen: Post-employment non-compete clauses are defined in your employment agreement and vary by seniority level: Senior Manager and above: 6-month non-compete for direct competitors in the same geography, Individual contributors: 3-month non-compete for roles with direct access to trade secrets. The company compensates non-compete periods with 50% of base salary for the duration. Non-solicitation (not hiring company employees or clients) applies for 12 months regardless of level. Violations may result in legal action and forfeiture of outstanding benefits.
rejected: There may be restrictions after you leave. Check your employment contract.

prompt: How do I request a workspace change (different floor or desk)?
chosen: Submit a workspace change request through the Facilities portal under Workspace > Seat Change Request with: reason (health, noise sensitivity, team alignment, accessibility needs), preferred location, and urgency. Facilities processes requests based on: space availability, department seating policies, team lead input, and medical requirements. Standard requests are fulfilled within 10-15 working days. Urgent requests (safety, harassment, accessibility) are prioritized within 48 hours. You cannot change workspaces without Facilities coordination.
rejected: Ask Facilities if you can move to a different desk.

prompt: Can I get additional training budget for my team?
chosen: Team training budget requests beyond the standard individual allocation are evaluated based on: team size, skill gap analysis, business criticality of the training, and department budget availability. Submit a Team Training Proposal to L&D (learning@company.com) including: training objectives, number of participants, estimated cost per person, expected ROI, and alternative delivery options (group rates, internal trainers vs. external). Proposals above $5,000 require department head approval. The decision timeline is 2-3 weeks.
rejected: Ask your manager about increasing the team's training budget.

prompt: What happens if I'm sick while on vacation?
chosen: If you fall ill during approved vacation leave: 1) Inform your manager and update your leave application, 2) For sick leave exceeding 3 consecutive days while on vacation, submit a medical certificate from a local doctor, 3) Those days may be converted from earned leave to sick leave (preserving your EL balance), 4) Travel insurance (provided for international trips) may cover medical expenses and trip interruption costs, 5) Unused vacation days due to illness cannot be re-added unless approved by HR on exceptional grounds.
rejected: If you get sick on vacation, those days might convert to sick leave.

prompt: Does the company provide legal assistance for personal matters?
chosen: The company's Employee Assistance Program (EAP) includes limited legal consultation: 1) Free 30-minute consultation with a licensed attorney for any legal issue (family, real estate, estate planning, consumer rights), 2) Discounted rates (20% below market) for ongoing legal representation through EAP partner firms, 3) Legal advice on workplace-specific issues (worker's compensation, employment disputes) is provided by company counsel, 4) The company does NOT cover personal legal expenses (court fees, attorney retainers for personal cases). Contact EAP for access to legal resources.
rejected: EAP includes some free legal consultation. Check their website.

prompt: What is the policy on employees receiving awards from external organizations?
chosen: Employees receiving external awards (industry recognition, conference speaking awards, community honors) are encouraged to inform HR for internal recognition and PR purposes. The company supports: 1) Paid time off to attend the award ceremony (up to 2 days), 2) Travel and accommodation expenses for the event (within travel policy limits), 3) Internal recognition through the newsletter and town hall announcement, 4) Reimbursement for nomination fees (if applicable). Awards must not conflict with company interests or use proprietary company information in the submission.
rejected: The company supports external awards. Tell HR if you receive one.

prompt: Can I request a temporary reduction in work hours?
chosen: Temporary work hour reduction is available through the Flexible Work Arrangement program: 1) Reduce to 80% (4 days/week) or 60% (3 days/week) schedule, 2) Duration: minimum 1 month, maximum 6 months, 3) Salary and benefits are prorated accordingly, 4) Eligibility: minimum 1 year of service, satisfactory performance, manager approval, 5) Common reasons: family care, health recovery, education, personal projects, 6) Request through HR Portal > Flexible Work with: proposed schedule, duration, reason, and coverage plan, 7) You can return to full-time before the term ends with 2 weeks notice.
rejected: You can request reduced hours. Talk to HR about options.

prompt: What is the company's policy on employees blogging or writing about work?
chosen: Employees may blog or write about their professional experience with these guidelines: 1) Do not disclose confidential information, unreleased product details, financial data, or internal strategies, 2) Do not use company proprietary data, customer names, or project specifics without written approval, 3) Clearly state that views expressed are personal and do not represent the company (add disclaimer), 4) Do not criticize the company, colleagues, or clients publicly, 5) Technical blogs about non-sensitive tools/technologies are generally encouraged, 6) If writing a book or being published, notify Corporate Communications. Personal blogging that violates these guidelines may result in disciplinary action.
rejected: You can blog about general experiences but don't share confidential info.

prompt: How do I handle a situation where a colleague is taking credit for my work?
chosen: If a colleague is claiming credit for your work: 1) Document your contribution (emails, version history, meeting notes, code commits, deliverables with timestamps), 2) Schedule a private conversation with the colleague to discuss the situation professionally, 3) If unresolved, escalate to your manager with evidence of your contribution, 4) For recurring issues, HR can facilitate mediation, 5) In team settings, proactively communicate your work updates in meetings and written status reports to establish visibility. The company values intellectual honesty and addresses credit appropriation seriously.
rejected: Document your work and talk to your manager about it.

prompt: What is the policy on employees running for public office?
chosen: Employees running for public office (local, state, or national) must: 1) Inform HR about their candidacy, 2) Comply with election laws regarding campaign activities (no company resources, time, or premises for campaigning), 3) Take unpaid leave during the active campaign period if the role requires significant time away from work, 4) Upon election, transition options include: continued employment with adjusted schedule (if compatible), sabbatical during the term, or resignation, 5) The company remains politically neutral and does not endorse candidates. Your employment is protected regardless of political outcome.
rejected: If you're running for office, tell HR and don't use company resources for campaigning.

prompt: Can I get my performance rating removed from my record?
chosen: Performance ratings are permanent records and cannot be removed. However: 1) If you successfully appealed a rating and it was revised, the original rating is marked as 'Overturned on Appeal' with the corrected rating displayed, 2) After 2 years, historical ratings are archived and only the most recent 2-3 ratings are considered for promotion/increment decisions, 3) You can add contextual comments to any rating explaining circumstances (medical issues, role changes, team disruptions) that affected performance, 4) Demonstrating significant improvement in subsequent cycles outweighs a single poor rating in career progression.
rejected: Ratings stay on your record. Focus on improving in future cycles.

prompt: What is the company's policy on employees having side businesses?
chosen: Side businesses are permitted under strict conditions: 1) Must not compete with the company's current or planned business, 2) Must not use company time, resources, equipment, or intellectual property, 3) Must not involve company clients, vendors, or employees during work hours, 4) Must not create a conflict of interest (actual or perceived), 5) Must be disclosed through the Conflict of Interest declaration form with details (business nature, time commitment, revenue), 6) Side businesses that interfere with job performance, require frequent work-hour attention, or damage company reputation will result in disciplinary action up to termination. Undisclosed businesses discovered are treated more severely.
rejected: Side businesses are okay if they don't conflict with company business. Disclose it to HR.

prompt: How does the company handle employee suggestions for cost savings?
chosen: Submit cost-saving suggestions through the Ideas Portal (accessible via the intranet) with: 1) Clear description of the idea, 2) Current state analysis with cost data, 3) Proposed solution with estimated savings, 4) Implementation timeline and resource requirements, 5) Potential risks or challenges. The Innovation Committee reviews submissions monthly. Approved ideas are implemented with the suggestor's involvement. Recognition includes: monetary reward (10% of first-year savings, capped at $5,000), public recognition at town hall, and consideration in performance reviews. The program has saved the company over $2M annually.
rejected: Submit cost-saving ideas through the Ideas Portal. You might get rewarded.

prompt: What is the policy on employees using company vehicles for personal use?
chosen: Company vehicles are for business use only unless a personal use allowance is explicitly stated in your employment package (typically Director grade and above). For employees with personal use privileges: 1) Personal use is limited to the employee and immediate family, 2) Fuel for personal trips is the employee's responsibility (company fuel card tracks business vs. personal), 3) The employee is liable for traffic violations and parking tickets during personal use, 4) Personal use must not exceed 1,000 km per month, 5) Vehicles must be used for commuting only if parking at home is secure. Unauthorized personal use by other employees is treated as misuse of company assets and may result in disciplinary action.
rejected: Company vehicles are for business use. Personal use requires specific approval.

prompt: Can I request an extension to my performance improvement plan deadline?
chosen: PIP extensions are granted in limited circumstances: 1) Documented medical issues that impacted your ability to perform during the PIP period, 2) Unforeseen business circumstances (project cancellation, team restructuring) that prevented you from demonstrating the required competencies, 3) A formal extension request to HR with supporting evidence, typically for an additional 30 days, 4) Your manager's recommendation for extension strengthens the request, 5) Extensions are not granted for: continued underperformance without valid reasons, lack of effort, or refusal to follow the PIP plan. If the extension is denied and PIP objectives are not met, separation may follow.
rejected: PIP extensions are rare. You'd need a valid reason like medical issues.

prompt: What is the company's policy on employees serving on external boards?
chosen: Employees serving on external boards (non-profit, industry associations, advisory boards, for-profit companies) must: 1) Obtain prior written approval from your manager and HR, 2) Ensure no conflict of interest with company business, 3) Not use company time, resources, or proprietary information for board activities, 4) Disclose any compensation received for board service, 5) Limit time commitment to no more than 4 hours per week during non-work hours (or as specified in approval), 6) Board service for competitors, clients, or vendors is prohibited. Approval is reviewed annually. Violations may result in termination.
rejected: You need HR approval to serve on external boards. Make sure there's no conflict.

prompt: How do I request a reference letter from the company?
chosen: Request a professional reference letter through HR Portal > Document Requests > Reference Letter. Specify the purpose (job application, university admission, professional certification, immigration) and the intended recipient. The letter includes: employment confirmation, designation, tenure, key responsibilities, and a general performance statement. For detailed references (specific achievements, skills assessment), your current or former manager is contacted to draft a personalized letter. Processing time: 5-7 working days for standard letters, 10 days for manager-drafted references.
rejected: Ask HR for a reference letter. They'll prepare one for you.

prompt: What is the company's policy on employee data privacy?
chosen: The company is committed to protecting employee personal data in compliance with GDPR, CCPA, and local privacy laws. Principles include: 1) Data is collected only for legitimate employment purposes, 2) Access is restricted to authorized personnel (HR, payroll, IT, managers with role-based access), 3) Data is retained only as long as legally required (employment records: 7 years post-separation), 4) You have the right to access, correct, or request deletion of your personal data (submit through HR Portal > Privacy Request), 5) Data breaches affecting employee information are reported within 72 hours, 6) Third-party vendors handling employee data are bound by data processing agreements. Annual privacy training is mandatory.
rejected: The company follows data privacy laws. Contact HR to access or correct your data.

prompt: Can I get reimbursement for a parking ticket I received at work?
chosen: Parking tickets are the employee's personal responsibility and are NOT reimbursed by the company, regardless of where they were issued (company parking lot, street parking near office, client site). Employees are expected to follow local parking regulations and use designated parking areas. Repeated parking violations at the company facility (3+ in a quarter) may result in: warning letter, suspension of parking privileges, or towing at employee's expense. If you believe a ticket was issued in error, dispute it directly with the issuing authority.
rejected: Parking tickets are your responsibility. The company doesn't reimburse them.

prompt: What happens if the company changes my role significantly?
changed: If your role changes significantly (new responsibilities, different skill requirements, reporting structure change), the company follows a structured process: 1) You receive written notification of the change with updated job description, 2) A meeting with your manager and HR to discuss the rationale, expectations, and support provided, 3) Training and onboarding for new responsibilities (up to 30 days), 4) Compensation adjustment if the role change represents a material increase in scope (assessed by HR Compensation team), 5) If you do not accept the change, HR explores alternative options within the organization, 6) If no alternative is available and you choose not to continue, separation terms are negotiated per your employment contract.
rejected: The company may change your role with notice. You can discuss it with HR.

prompt: How do I report a health and safety violation at a client site?
chosen: Report health and safety violations at client sites immediately: 1) Remove yourself from the hazardous situation if there is immediate danger, 2) Inform your manager and the company's Health & Safety team (safety@company.com or ext. 6666), 3) Document the violation with photos (if safe), date, time, location, and specific concerns, 4) The company escalates the issue to the client's management and requests corrective action, 5) If the client does not address the violation, the company may suspend work at that site until it is safe, 6) You are fully protected from retaliation for reporting safety concerns. Your safety takes priority over client relationships.
rejected: Report safety issues at client sites to your manager and the Safety team.

prompt: Can I use my learning budget for personal development courses?
chosen: Your annual $2,000 learning budget is intended for job-related and career development. Personal development courses are eligible if they contribute to soft skills, leadership, communication, emotional intelligence, time management, or other competencies relevant to workplace performance. Examples of approved personal development: public speaking workshops, negotiation courses, mindfulness training, personality assessments (MBTI, DiSC), coaching certifications. Courses purely for personal hobbies (cooking classes, art workshops) are not covered. Submit through the LMS with a brief justification linking the course to your professional growth.
rejected: Learning budget is for job-related courses mostly. Personal development might be okay.

prompt: What is the company's policy on employee protests or strikes?
chosen: The company respects employees' legal rights to peaceful protest and collective action as per applicable labor laws. However: 1) Protests must not occur on company premises or during work hours, 2) Company resources (email, printers, meeting rooms) cannot be used for organizing protests, 3) Employees must not coerce or pressure colleagues into participating, 4) Participation in legal strikes is protected from retaliation, 5) Unprotected work stoppages (wildcat strikes) may result in disciplinary action, 6) The company encourages resolving grievances through established channels (town halls, surveys, HR discussions) before considering collective action. Legal advice is available through EAP.
rejected: Employees have rights to protest but not during work hours or on company premises.

prompt: How do I handle a conflict between my religious practices and work schedule?
chosen: If your religious practices conflict with work requirements, request a religious accommodation through HR: 1) Schedule a confidential meeting with your HR Business Partner, 2) Explain the religious requirement (prayer times, Sabbath observance, holy days, dietary restrictions, dress code), 3) Propose a reasonable accommodation (schedule adjustment, flexible breaks, workspace modification), 4) HR works with your manager to assess feasibility and implement the accommodation within 15 working days, 5) Accommodations that cause undue hardship (significant operational disruption or cost) may require alternative solutions. The company is committed to respecting religious diversity and finds solutions in good faith.
rejected: Talk to HR about accommodating your religious needs.

prompt: What is the policy on employees creating intellectual property outside of work?
chosen: Intellectual property created outside of work hours, without company resources, and unrelated to company business belongs to you. However: 1) If the IP relates to your job responsibilities, uses company information, or was conceived during employment with company resources, it may be considered company property per your IP assignment agreement, 2) You must disclose outside inventions through the IP Disclosure form to clarify ownership, 3) Patents, copyrights, or trademarks filed for outside IP must not reference company affiliation without authorization, 4) Company name, logo, or reputation cannot be used to promote personal IP, 5) If there is ambiguity, the Legal team conducts an assessment. Early disclosure prevents disputes.
rejected: IP you create outside work is yours if it doesn't relate to company business or use company resources.

prompt: Can I get financial assistance for childcare?
chosen: Childcare financial support includes: 1) On-site daycare subsidized at 50% of market rate ($500/month vs. $1,000), 2) Emergency backup childcare (10 days/year at company expense), 3) Childcare Flexible Spending Account (FSA) — pre-tax contributions up to $5,000/year for eligible childcare expenses, 4) School admission assistance in company-partnered schools (5-10% discount), 5) Summer camp vouchers (up to $200/child/year), 6) Nursing mother support (lactation rooms, breast pump reimbursement up to $300), 7) Flexible work arrangements during school holidays. Apply through the Benefits portal with childcare provider details and cost breakdown.
rejected: The company offers some childcare benefits. Check the benefits portal.

prompt: What happens if I'm selected for jury duty?
chosen: Jury duty is a civic obligation fully supported by the company: 1) Submit the jury summons to HR within 3 days of receipt, 2) You receive paid jury duty leave for the entire duration of service, 3) Your salary continues at the normal rate, 4) Any jury compensation (fees, mileage) received from the court is yours to keep — the company does not deduct it from your salary, 5) If the trial extends beyond the initial summons period, provide updated dates to HR, 6) You are expected to return to work on days when court is not in session, 7) If selected for a lengthy trial (months), discuss with HR about long-term leave arrangements.
rejected: You get paid leave for jury duty. Just inform HR when you receive the summons.

prompt: How do I address a situation where I'm being excluded from team activities?
chosen: If you feel excluded from team activities, meetings, or social interactions: 1) Document specific instances (dates, events, who was included, impact on your work), 2) Have a candid conversation with your manager about the pattern and how it affects your ability to contribute, 3) If the exclusion is deliberate (bullying, isolation tactics), report to HR for investigation, 4) Request to be included in recurring meeting invites and team communication channels, 5) HR can facilitate a team discussion about inclusive behavior and collaboration norms, 6) For persistent exclusion or retaliatory behavior, a formal grievance can be filed. Inclusive teamwork is a company value and taken seriously.
rejected: Talk to your manager if you feel left out. HR can also help.

prompt: What is the company's policy on employees being arrested or charged with a crime?
chosen: If you are arrested or charged with a crime: 1) You must inform HR within 48 hours of the arrest or charge, 2) The company conducts an individualized assessment considering: nature of the charge, relevance to your role, impact on company reputation, and employment status (pre-trial vs. convicted), 3) Pre-trial: you may be placed on paid administrative leave pending the outcome, 4) Conviction for offenses involving violence, fraud, or moral turpitude may result in termination, 5) Minor offenses (traffic violations, misdemeanors unrelated to work) typically do not affect employment, 6) All information is kept confidential and used only for employment decisions. Legal support is available through EAP.
rejected: You must inform HR if you're arrested. The company will assess the situation.

prompt: Can I request a copy of all personal data the company holds about me?
chosen: Yes, you have the right to request a complete copy of your personal data held by the company (Subject Access Request under GDPR or equivalent): 1) Submit a request through HR Portal > Privacy > Data Access Request, 2) Specify the scope (all data, specific systems, particular time period), 3) The company responds within 30 days with: employment records, performance reviews, compensation data, attendance records, benefits information, training history, IT logs, and communications stored in company systems, 4) Data is provided in a machine-readable format (CSV, JSON, or PDF), 5) Third-party data (references, background checks) is included with appropriate consent, 6) Requests can be made once per quarter without charge; excessive requests may incur administrative fees.
rejected: Yes, you can request your personal data. Submit a privacy request to HR.

prompt: What is the policy on employees using company printers for personal documents?
chosen: Occasional personal printing (up to 20 pages per month) is permitted on company printers for non-commercial purposes. Limitations: 1) No printing of copyrighted material for distribution, 2) No printing of offensive, illegal, or inappropriate content, 3) Personal printing exceeding 20 pages/month is charged to the employee at cost ($0.10/page B&W, $0.50/page color), 4) Large personal print jobs (theses, books) require manager approval, 5) The company reserves the right to monitor print logs for policy violations. Excessive personal use may result in printing privileges being revoked.
rejected: Light personal printing is okay. Heavy use may be charged to you.

prompt: How do I handle a situation where I disagree with a company policy?
chosen: If you disagree with a company policy: 1) Review the policy document to ensure you understand the rationale and full context, 2) Discuss your concerns with your manager or HR Business Partner to get clarification, 3) Submit formal feedback through the Policy Feedback form on the HR portal (anonymous option available), 4) Participate in town hall Q&A sessions where policies are discussed, 5) If you are part of an Employee Resource Group or committee, raise the concern through that channel for collective representation, 6) While policies are designed for the organization's needs, the company values employee input and periodically reviews policies based on feedback. However, policies must be followed until officially revised.
rejected: Share your feedback with HR or through the policy feedback form.

prompt: What is the company's policy on employee testimonials or case studies?
chosen: The company occasionally features employee testimonials in marketing materials, recruitment campaigns, and case studies. Participation is entirely voluntary: 1) You will be contacted by Corporate Communications or Talent Acquisition with a specific request, 2) You can decline without any consequence, 3) If you agree, the content (quotes, photos, video) is reviewed and approved by you before publication, 4) You can request removal of your testimonial at any time, 5) Compensation is not provided for testimonials as they are considered part of professional visibility, 6) External media requests for interviews are referred to Corporate Communications. You are not authorized to speak on behalf of the company to media without explicit approval.
rejected: You may be asked for testimonials. Participation is voluntary.

prompt: What is the policy on employees accepting speaking engagements at conferences?
chosen: Employees are encouraged to speak at industry conferences as it builds personal and company visibility. Guidelines: 1) Inform your manager and Corporate Communications about the speaking engagement, 2) Do not disclose confidential information, unreleased products, financial data, or client details, 3) The presentation must not endorse competitors or criticize the company, 4) If using the company name in promotional materials, get approval from Corporate Communications, 5) Conference attendance costs (registration, travel) may be covered by the company if pre-approved as professional development, 6) Speaking fees/honorariums are yours to keep, 7) The company may request a copy of your presentation for internal review before the event.
rejected: You can speak at conferences. Just don't share confidential info and tell your manager.

prompt: Can I request a change in my performance review cycle?
chosen: Performance review cycles are standardized across the organization (mid-year: June-July, annual: December-January) and individual cycle changes are not permitted. However: 1) If you recently changed roles or departments, your review may be aligned with the new team's schedule, 2) For employees on extended leave (sabbatical, medical) during review period, reviews are conducted upon return, 3) If you joined mid-cycle, your first review is prorated to the next full cycle, 4) You can request an off-cycle career discussion with your manager (not a formal review) to address specific concerns or goal adjustments.
rejected: Review cycles are fixed. You can't change them individually.

prompt: How do I handle a situation where I discover a payroll overpayment?
chosen: If you notice an overpayment in your salary: 1) Do not spend the excess amount, 2) Notify the Payroll team immediately (payroll@company.com or ext. 5555), 3) Payroll investigates and confirms whether it was an error, 4) If confirmed, the overpayment is recovered through salary deduction: overpayments under $500 are recovered in one installment, $500-$2,000 over 2-3 months, over $2,000 over 3-6 months (to minimize hardship), 5) You will receive a written notification of the recovery schedule, 6) If you are leaving the company, the outstanding amount is deducted from your full and final settlement. Honest reporting is appreciated and not penalized.
rejected: Report overpayments to payroll. They'll recover it from your salary.

prompt: What is the company's policy on employees using AI tools for work?
chosen: The company encourages responsible use of AI tools to enhance productivity while maintaining security and quality standards: 1) Only use company-approved AI tools (listed on the IT portal) — unauthorized AI tools may send company data to external servers, 2) Do NOT input confidential company data, customer information, proprietary code, or financial data into external AI services without IT Security approval, 3) AI-generated outputs must be reviewed for accuracy, bias, and completeness before use in official communications or deliverables, 4) AI should augment, not replace, human judgment and expertise, 5) Disclose AI use in significant deliverables (reports, code, customer communications) where relevant, 6) Regular AI literacy training is provided. Violations (e.g., sharing confidential data with AI tools) may result in disciplinary action.
rejected: Use approved AI tools and don't put confidential data in them.

prompt: Can I get reimbursement for a professional certification exam I already passed?
chosen: Yes, the company reimburses certification exam fees for job-related certifications even if you took the exam before formal approval, provided: 1) The certification is on the approved list (AWS, Azure, GCP, PMP, CISSP, SHRM, etc.), 2) You passed the exam (failed exams are not reimbursed), 3) Submit a reimbursement request through the Expense portal within 30 days of passing, 4) Include: exam receipt, certificate or score report, and a brief statement of relevance to your role, 5) Manager approval is required, 6) Reimbursement covers: exam fee, study materials (up to $200), and one retake if needed. Processing time is 7-10 business days.
rejected: Yes, you can get reimbursed if you passed and the cert is relevant.

prompt: What happens if I'm unable to return to work after an extended medical leave?
chosen: If you cannot return to work after exhausting your medical leave (typically 90-180 days): 1) HR and your manager discuss your status and prognosis, 2) Additional unpaid medical leave (up to 90 more days) may be granted if there is a reasonable expectation of recovery, 3) If you are permanently unable to perform your role, the company explores alternative roles with reduced physical/cognitive requirements (reasonable accommodation), 4) If no suitable role exists and you are permanently disabled, the employment may be terminated on medical grounds with: full severance package, extended health insurance (6 months), disability benefits payout (if enrolled), and outplacement support, 5) All medical information is kept strictly confidential.
rejected: If you can't return after medical leave, the company will discuss options with you.

prompt: How do I raise a concern about unethical behavior by a senior leader?
chosen: Concerns about senior leaders require careful handling due to the power dynamic. Reporting options: 1) Anonymous ethics hotline (24/7, operated by a third-party, cannot be traced back to you), 2) Direct report to the Chief Ethics Officer or General Counsel (skip all management layers), 3) Report to the Board of Directors' Audit Committee (for serious allegations like fraud, harassment, regulatory violations), 4) Direct confidential conversation with your HR Business Partner (who escalates without revealing your identity). The company's non-retaliation policy applies even more strongly for reports about senior leaders. All investigations are conducted by independent parties to ensure impartiality.
rejected: Use the anonymous ethics hotline to report concerns about senior leaders.

prompt: What is the company's policy on employees taking vacation during probation?
chosen: Vacation during probation is permitted but with limitations: 1) Your leave entitlement is prorated from your joining date (e.g., after 3 months of a 6-month probation, you have half the annual leave balance), 2) Planned vacation (applied before joining) is honored — disclose during onboarding so arrangements can be made, 3) Vacation exceeding 5 consecutive working days during probation extends the probation period by the same duration, 4) Emergency leave (sick, family) does not extend probation, 5) Frequent or extended leave during probation may affect the confirmation decision if it impacts learning and performance. Discuss any planned leave with your manager and HR in advance.
rejected: You can take leave during probation but it might extend your probation period.

prompt: Can I request a change in my tax filing status mid-year?
chosen: Tax filing status changes (e.g., marital status change, dependent additions) can be updated mid-year through HR Portal > Tax > Life Event Update within 30 days of the qualifying event: 1) Submit supporting documents (marriage certificate, birth certificate, adoption papers), 2) The tax withholding is recalculated from the month following the update, 3) If the change results in lower tax withholding, any shortfall is recovered at year-end (February-March), 4) Changes made outside the 30-day window take effect from the next quarter, 5) Consult with a tax advisor (available through EAP) to understand the impact before making changes. You can also adjust voluntary tax declarations at any time.
rejected: You can update tax status after major life events. Submit documents to HR.

prompt: What is the policy on employees sharing office space with external parties?
chosen: Sharing company office space with external parties (freelancers, contractors, partner organizations, acquired companies) is permitted with prior approval: 1) Submit a request to Facilities and IT Security with: party details, duration, purpose, and access requirements, 2) External parties must sign an NDA and comply with company security policies, 3) IT provisions: temporary access badges, guest Wi-Fi (not internal network), no access to company systems unless explicitly approved, 4) Duration: short-term (up to 30 days, manager approval), long-term (up to 6 months, department head + IT Security approval), 5) External parties are not entitled to company amenities (cafeteria subsidy, gym) unless specified in the agreement, 6) All shared space arrangements are reviewed quarterly for security compliance.
rejected: External parties can use office space with approval. They need to sign an NDA.

prompt: How do I handle a situation where I'm asked to work in unsafe conditions?
chosen: You have the right to refuse work in unsafe conditions without fear of retaliation: 1) Immediately inform your manager and the Safety team (safety@company.com or ext. 6666) about the specific hazard, 2) Do not attempt the work until the hazard is assessed and resolved, 3) The Safety team conducts an investigation within 2 hours for urgent hazards, 4) If the hazard is confirmed, work is suspended or relocated until the issue is fixed, 5) If your manager insists you proceed despite safety concerns, escalate to HR, the Safety Director, or the anonymous ethics hotline, 6) The company complies with OSHA and local workplace safety regulations. Your health and safety take priority over deadlines or productivity.
rejected: Don't work in unsafe conditions. Report it to Safety and your manager.

prompt: What is the company's policy on employees writing books or publishing content?
chosen: Employees are supported in writing books, articles, or other published content with these guidelines: 1) The content must not include confidential company information, trade secrets, unreleased product details, or client data, 2) If the book relates to your area of work at the company, notify HR and Corporate Communications, 3) The company may provide: professional editing support, foreword by leadership, marketing through company channels, paid time off for writing (up to 5 days/year), 4) Royalties and earnings from the book are yours — the company claims no ownership, 5) If you use company resources (research, data, images), prior approval is required, 6) The company may request to review the manuscript before publication to ensure no confidential information is disclosed.
rejected: You can write books as long as you don't share confidential company info.

prompt: Can I get compensation for unused vacation when I leave the company?
chosen: Upon separation, unused earned leave (EL) is encashed at your Basic Pay rate as part of the full and final settlement. Calculation: (Unused EL days) × (Monthly Basic / 30). Maximum encashable balance is 45 days (any excess is encashed at year-end automatically). Casual leave and sick leave are NOT encashable. Leave encashment is paid within 45 days of your last working day along with your final salary, gratuity (if eligible), and any pending reimbursements. Note: if you are terminated for misconduct, leave encashment may be forfeited per company policy and local labor laws.
rejected: Unused earned leave is encashed when you leave. Casual and sick leave are not.

prompt: What is the company's policy on employees recording conversations?
chosen: Recording conversations (audio, video) in the workplace requires consent of all parties involved: 1) For business meetings, the organizer must announce recording at the start and give attendees the option to leave, 2) One-on-one conversations require explicit verbal consent before recording, 3) Secret recordings (without consent) are a violation of privacy and company policy, potentially resulting in termination, 4) Approved recordings are stored on company systems for 90 days unless explicitly archived, 5) Recordings must not be shared externally without approval from Corporate Communications and Legal, 6) Exception: recording for accessibility purposes (transcription for hearing-impaired employees) is permitted with prior HR approval.
rejected: Don't record conversations without everyone's consent. It's a privacy violation.

prompt: How do I request a mentorship relationship through the company program?
chosen: Apply for the mentorship program through HR Portal > Learning > Mentorship Program: 1) Complete a mentorship application indicating your goals, areas for development, and preferred mentor characteristics (seniority, expertise, background), 2) The program runs in 6-month cycles (January-June, July-December), 3) Applications are reviewed by the Mentorship Committee who matches mentors and mentees based on compatibility and goals, 4) Matches are announced within 2 weeks of the application deadline, 5) Pairs meet bi-weekly (minimum 1 hour) with suggested discussion topics provided, 6) Both parties can request a rematch if the relationship is not productive, 7) Successful completion is recognized with certificates and counts toward your professional development record.
rejected: Apply for the mentorship program through the learning portal.

prompt: What happens if I violate the company's code of conduct?
chosen: Code of conduct violations are addressed through a progressive discipline process based on severity: 1) Minor violations (dress code, minor tardiness, casual policy breaches): verbal or written warning, coaching, 2) Moderate violations (repeated minor violations, unauthorized overtime, misuse of company resources): written warning, mandatory training, possible suspension (1-3 days unpaid), 3) Serious violations (harassment, fraud, data breach, discrimination, conflict of interest): investigation, possible demotion, suspension (up to 2 weeks), or immediate termination, 4) Criminal violations (theft, violence, insider trading): termination plus referral to law enforcement, 5) All violations are documented in your personnel file. You have the right to respond to allegations and appeal disciplinary decisions through the grievance process.
rejected: Violations range from warnings to termination depending on severity.

prompt: What is the company policy on employees receiving stock options?
chosen: Stock options (ESOPs) are granted based on grade level and performance: eligibility starts at Senior Associate grade with consistent 'Exceeds Expectations' or higher ratings. Grants are made annually during the ESOP cycle (typically Q1). Vesting follows a 4-year schedule with 25% vesting each year on the grant anniversary. Exercise price is the fair market value at grant date. Options must be exercised within 90 days of vesting (or within 90 days of separation for vested options). Unvested options are forfeited upon separation. Details of your grants, vesting status, and exercise procedures are available on the ESOP portal.
rejected: Stock options are granted based on performance. Check the ESOP portal for details.

prompt: Can I work part-time while on sick leave?
chosen: Working while on sick leave is contradictory and not permitted. Sick leave is granted when you are medically unfit to work, and performing work duties undermines that status. If you feel well enough to work part-time: 1) Consult your doctor about fitness for work, 2) If cleared for limited duties, discuss with HR about a phased return (reduced hours, WFH, lighter workload), 3) Return to work officially and utilize flexible work arrangements, 4) Do NOT check emails, attend meetings, or perform any work tasks while officially on sick leave. Doing so may result in sick leave being converted to regular leave and could affect insurance claims.
rejected: You shouldn't work while on sick leave. If you're well enough, return to work.

prompt: What is the policy on employees giving gifts to managers?
chosen: Gifts from employees to managers are discouraged to avoid the perception of favoritism or influence. If you wish to show appreciation: 1) Group gifts from the entire team (under $25 per person) for occasions like Manager Appreciation Day or farewells are acceptable, 2) Handwritten thank-you notes are always appropriate and encouraged, 3) Individual gifts above $50 must be declined by the manager and reported to HR, 4) Cash or cash-equivalent gifts (gift cards) are never acceptable in either direction, 5) Managers must report any gifts received to their skip-level manager. The company encourages recognition through formal channels (peer recognition portal, performance feedback) rather than gifts.
rejected: It's better not to give gifts to your manager. A thank-you note is enough.

prompt: How do I handle a dispute with HR about my benefits?
chosen: If you have a dispute with HR regarding benefits eligibility, coverage, or entitlements: 1) Request a formal meeting with your HR Business Partner to discuss the specific issue with documentation (policy documents, employment contract, benefit plan details), 2) If unresolved, escalate to the Benefits Manager or HR Director with a written summary of the dispute, 3) For insurance-related disputes, contact the insurance provider directly to understand policy terms, 4) For legal interpretation of benefits, the company provides free legal consultation through EAP, 5) As a final resort, file a formal grievance through the Grievance Portal for independent investigation, 6) Benefits disputes are typically resolved within 30 days. Your benefits are not affected during the dispute resolution process.
rejected: Discuss the benefits dispute with your HRBP and escalate if needed.

prompt: What is the company's policy on employees being promoted to manage former peers?
chosen: When promoted to manage former peers, the company provides structured support: 1) A transition meeting with the new manager and team facilitated by HR to address the change openly, 2) Clear communication about the selection rationale and expectations, 3) The new manager receives 'Managing Former Peers' training within 30 days, 4) One-on-one conversations with each team member to establish new working dynamics, 5) Any team member uncomfortable with the change can request a confidential discussion with HR, 6) A 90-day check-in assesses how the transition is progressing, 7) If conflicts arise, HR provides mediation. Professionalism and respect from all parties are expected during the transition.
rejected: HR helps with the transition when you manage former peers.

prompt: Can I request an early performance review if I feel I've exceeded expectations?
chosen: Formal performance reviews follow the standardized cycle (mid-year and annual) and cannot be requested individually. However: 1) You can request an off-cycle career discussion with your manager to highlight achievements and discuss growth, 2) If you believe your role has significantly expanded, request a role and compensation review through HR (separate from performance review), 3) Document your achievements continuously and share them in regular 1-on-1s so they're considered during the formal review, 4) For exceptional circumstances (promotion-ready well before cycle, market adjustment needed), your manager can initiate an early review with HR and department head approval, 5) Spot bonuses and recognition can be given anytime independent of the review cycle.
rejected: Reviews happen on schedule. You can discuss achievements with your manager anytime.

prompt: What is the company's policy on employees serving as expert witnesses?
chosen: Employees subpoenaed to serve as expert witnesses must: 1) Notify HR and the Legal team immediately upon receiving the subpoena, 2) The company provides paid time off for court appearances, 3) If the expert testimony relates to your work at the company, the Legal team prepares you and may be present, 4) If the testimony is about personal expertise unrelated to company business, you may serve in your personal capacity (unpaid or with court compensation), 5) You must not disclose confidential company information in testimony without Legal approval, 6) The company supports civic duty and does not penalize employees for witness service.
rejected: If subpoenaed as a witness, tell HR and Legal. You'll get time off.

prompt: How do I deal with a toxic team member affecting morale?
chosen: Address toxic team behavior through these steps: 1) Document specific instances (dates, behaviors, impact on team, witnesses), focusing on observable actions not personality, 2) If safe, have a direct conversation with the individual about the impact of their behavior, 3) Escalate to your manager with documented examples — managers are responsible for team culture, 4) For persistent issues, HR can facilitate team coaching or individual counseling through EAP, 5) If the behavior constitutes harassment, bullying, or discrimination, file a formal grievance for investigation, 6) As a manager, address toxic behavior immediately through coaching, performance management, or disciplinary action. Ignoring toxic behavior signals tolerance and worsens team morale.
rejected: Document toxic behavior and report it to your manager or HR.

prompt: What is the company's policy on employees requesting references for personal matters?
chosen: The company provides references for personal matters (apartment rental, loan applications, visa applications, professional licensing) upon request: 1) Submit a Reference Request through HR Portal > Document Requests specifying the purpose, recipient, and information needed, 2) Standard employment verification (dates, designation, salary) is provided within 2-3 working days, 3) Character references or detailed performance references require manager involvement and take 5-7 working days, 4) For financial references (loans, mortgages), salary and employment confirmation is provided with your written consent, 5) References are issued on company letterhead with authorized signature, 6) The company does not provide subjective opinions in references — only factual, verifiable information.
rejected: HR can provide references for personal matters. Submit a request through the portal.

prompt: What happens if I accidentally violate a company policy?
chosen: Accidental policy violations are handled with consideration for intent and impact: 1) Report the violation immediately to your manager or HR — honesty demonstrates integrity, 2) The company assesses: was it truly unintentional, what was the impact, have you violated this policy before, did you take steps to mitigate the impact, 3) For first-time, genuine accidents with minimal impact: coaching and policy education (no formal discipline), 4) For repeated accidental violations: written reminder and mandatory re-training, 5) If the accident caused significant harm (data breach, financial loss, safety issue): formal investigation and appropriate disciplinary action, 6) The company values transparency — employees who self-report are treated more leniently than those whose violations are discovered.
rejected: Report accidental violations immediately. First-time honest mistakes are usually just coached.

prompt: Can I take leave during my notice period?
chosen: Leave during notice period is generally not permitted unless approved by your manager and HR. The notice period is intended for knowledge transfer and handover. If you have urgent personal matters, you may request to adjust your last working date or take unpaid leave for specific days with documented justification. Any unused leave balance will be encashed as per company policy upon separation. Discuss your specific situation with HR to explore options.
rejected: You probably can't take leave during notice period. Talk to HR.

prompt: What happens to my leave balance if I'm on long-term sick leave?
chosen: During long-term sick leave (medical leave exceeding 30 days), your earned leave and casual leave continue to accrue as per standard policy. However, casual leave cannot be accumulated during sick leave — it continues to lapse on December 31st. Earned leave accrues normally and can be used after you return to work. If your sick leave extends beyond 90 days, HR will conduct a welfare check and discuss your return-to-work plan. Your leave balance is protected during approved medical leave.
rejected: Your leave keeps accumulating. Don't worry about it.

prompt: Can I donate my leave balance to a colleague?
chosen: Leave donation is permitted through the company's Leave Donation Program for employees facing medical emergencies or natural disasters. You can donate up to 5 days of earned leave per year to eligible colleagues. The recipient must have exhausted their own leave balance and provide medical documentation or disaster proof. Donations are processed through HR with both parties' written consent. Donated leave cannot be returned to the donor and must be used within 6 months by the recipient.
rejected: Some companies allow leave donation. Check if ours does.

prompt: I missed punching in for 5 days. What should I do?
chosen: Missing attendance punches for 5 consecutive days requires immediate regularization. Log into the HR portal and raise 5 separate 'Missed Punch' requests under Attendance > Regularization, each with: actual arrival/departure times, manager approval, and reason for missing punches. You have 48 hours per day to regularize. If beyond 48 hours, your manager must escalate to HR. Note: You're allowed maximum 3 missed punch regularizations per month. Exceeding this may result in half-day leave deductions for unverified days.
rejected: Just mark your attendance late on the portal.

prompt: Can I work from a different office location temporarily?
chosen: Temporary inter-office transfers (working from a different company office in another city) require 2 weeks advance notice. Submit an 'Inter-Office Work Request' through the Facilities portal with: your current location, desired location, duration (max 30 days per quarter), manager approval, and business justification. The receiving office must confirm desk availability. Your attendance will be tracked via the receiving office's biometric system. Extended periods beyond 30 days require HR approval and may be treated as a permanent transfer.
rejected: You can probably work from another office. Ask your manager.

prompt: How is overtime calculated for salaried employees?
chosen: Salaried employees are not eligible for overtime pay as per their employment classification. However, if you work more than 50 hours in a week consistently (4+ weeks), you should discuss workload concerns with your manager. The company encourages work-life balance and may offer compensatory time off (comp-off) for weekend work with prior manager approval. Comp-offs must be availed within 30 days and cannot be encashed. Track extra hours through the Attendance portal and discuss comp-off eligibility with your manager.
rejected: Salaried employees don't get overtime. You're expected to work as needed.

prompt: My salary is delayed this month. Who do I contact?
chosen: Salary is typically credited on the last working day of the month. If delayed beyond 2 business days: 1) Check the HR portal for any announcements about payroll delays, 2) Verify your bank account details are correct in the portal, 3) Contact the Payroll team at payroll@company.com with your employee ID and specific concern, 4) If the issue is a missing bank update, submit corrected details immediately. The company aims to resolve payroll issues within 3 business days. For urgent financial hardship due to delayed salary, HR can arrange an emergency advance.
rejected: Wait a few days. If it doesn't come, email HR.

prompt: Can I change my tax declaration after the start of the financial year?
chosen: Tax declarations can be revised once per financial year before the Q3 payroll cut-off (typically December 31st). Log into the Payroll portal > Tax Declaration > Revise Declaration to update: investment declarations, HRA claims, home loan interest, or other tax-saving instruments. After December 31st, no further revisions are allowed for that financial year — any missed declarations will result in higher TDS. You can claim actual expenses during annual tax filing (Form 16) even if not declared earlier. Submit investment proofs by the deadline specified by the Payroll team.
rejected: You can change tax declarations once a year. Check the payroll portal.

prompt: What deductions are mandatory from my salary?
chosen: Mandatory salary deductions include: 1) Income Tax (TDS) as per your tax slab and declarations, 2) Provident Fund (12% of basic salary — employee contribution matched by employer), 3) Professional Tax (varies by state, typically ₹200/month), 4) Employee State Insurance (ESI) if gross salary is below ₹21,000/month (0.75% employee contribution), 5) Any court-ordered garnishments or loan EMIs if you have active company loans. Optional deductions include: health insurance premium (if opted), gym membership, meal card top-ups. View all deductions in your monthly payslip on the Payroll portal.
rejected: Tax, PF, and other standard deductions. Check your payslip.

prompt: Can I add my parents to the company health insurance?
chosen: Yes, you can add parents (both biological and in-law) to the company health insurance as dependents. The base policy covers you, spouse, and 2 children automatically. Adding parents requires: 1) Submit parent details through the Benefits portal within 30 days of joining or during annual enrollment, 2) Pay an additional premium of $150/month per parent (deducted from salary), 3) Parents must be under 65 years at enrollment (existing coverage continues until 70), 4) Pre-existing conditions have a 2-year waiting period. Once added, parents cannot be removed until annual enrollment. Claims are processed through the same insurance provider portal.
rejected: You might be able to add parents. Check with the insurance provider.

prompt: What is the company's gym reimbursement policy?
chosen: The company reimburses up to $50/month for gym or fitness center membership as part of the Employee Wellness Program. Eligibility: 1) Full-time employees after 90-day probation, 2) Membership must be at a registered fitness center (list available on Benefits portal), 3) Submit monthly reimbursement request with: original receipt, membership proof, and attendance log (minimum 8 visits/month), 4) Reimbursement is processed with next month's salary, 5) Online fitness platforms (Peloton, Nike Training Club) are also eligible. Maximum annual reimbursement is $600. Unused monthly balance does not carry forward.
rejected: The company reimburses some gym costs. Submit your receipts.

prompt: Does the company provide education assistance for my children?
chosen: The company offers a Children's Education Assistance program for employees at Manager grade and above with 3+ years of service. Benefits: 1) Up to $1,000/year per child (maximum 2 children), 2) Covers tuition fees, textbooks, and school supplies, 3) Children must be between ages 5-18 and enrolled in a recognized school, 4) Submit education bills and report cards through the Benefits portal by December 31st each year, 5) Assistance is reimbursed in January of the following year. This is separate from your personal learning budget. Part-time and contract employees are not eligible.
rejected: Some companies offer education benefits. Ask HR if we do.

prompt: What happens if I fail my PIP (Performance Improvement Plan)?
chosen: If you fail to meet PIP objectives within the specified timeline (typically 60-90 days): 1) HR and your manager will review documented performance gaps, 2) You'll be invited to a formal performance discussion, 3) Possible outcomes include: extension of PIP with revised goals (rare), role reassignment to a more suitable position, or termination of employment, 4) If termination is decided, you'll receive notice period pay and separation benefits as per policy, 5) You have the right to present additional evidence or context during the review. HR ensures all decisions are documented and non-discriminatory. Seek clarification from HR about your specific PIP terms.
rejected: If you fail the PIP, you might get fired. Talk to your manager.

prompt: Can I appeal my performance rating?
chosen: Yes, you can appeal your performance rating within 15 days of the official rating communication. The appeal process: 1) Submit a written appeal to HR with specific grounds: factual errors in evaluation, bias, or comparison with incorrect peer group, 2) Provide supporting evidence: completed projects, client feedback, metrics, 3) An independent reviewer (senior leader from another department) will review your case, 4) The reviewer's decision is final and binding, 5) Appeals are confidential and will not affect future evaluations. Approximately 10% of appeals result in rating changes. Discuss concerns with your manager before escalating to formal appeal.
rejected: You can appeal but it's unlikely to change. Check with HR.

prompt: How does the promotion cycle work?
chosen: Promotions are evaluated during the annual review cycle (January-March): 1) Managers nominate high-performing employees based on: consistent 'Exceeds Expectations' ratings for 2+ years, demonstrated readiness for next level, and business need, 2) Nominations are reviewed by a Promotion Committee (department head, HR, and cross-functional leaders), 3) Candidates may be interviewed or assessed for role readiness, 4) Decisions are communicated in March, with compensation changes effective April 1st, 5) Promotions are not guaranteed even with strong performance — business needs and budget constraints apply, 6) Employees at the same level for 4+ years receive a 'career path review' with HR. Self-nominations are not accepted.
rejected: Promotions happen once a year. Your manager will nominate you if you're doing well.

prompt: Can I work remotely from another country?
chosen: Working remotely from another country (international remote work) is permitted for up to 30 days per year with advance approval: 1) Submit an 'International Remote Work Request' 60 days before travel through the HR portal, 2) Specify destination country, duration, and business justification, 3) Approval depends on: time zone overlap (minimum 4 hours with your team), local labor law compliance, and data security regulations, 4) You remain on your current compensation (no location adjustment), 5) Some countries are restricted due to sanctions or data laws (HR provides list), 6) Beyond 30 days, you may need a local employment contract and work visa. Tax implications should be discussed with the Tax team.
rejected: You can work from abroad for a short time. Get manager approval.

prompt: What equipment does the company provide for remote work?
chosen: For approved remote/hybrid work, the company provides: 1) Laptop (company-issued, replaced every 3 years), 2) Monitor (up to $300 reimbursement), 3) Ergonomic chair (up to $200 reimbursement with receipt), 4) Desk setup accessories (keyboard, mouse, webcam — up to $100 total), 5) Internet subsidy of $50/month, 6) Company VPN and software licenses. Submit equipment requests through the IT portal under 'Remote Work Setup.' Reimbursements require pre-approval and original receipts. Equipment remains company property and must be returned upon separation. Damage beyond normal wear may result in deduction from final settlement.
rejected: The company gives you a laptop and some money for equipment. Check the IT portal.

prompt: Are remote employees required to be online during specific hours?
chosen: Remote employees must maintain core availability hours: 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM in your local time zone for collaboration, meetings, and real-time communication. Outside core hours, you have flexibility to structure your 8-hour workday (e.g., 8 AM-5 PM or 11 AM-8 PM with 1-hour lunch). Requirements: 1) Be reachable on company chat/phone during core hours (response within 15 minutes), 2) Attend scheduled team meetings, 3) Update your status on the company chat tool, 4) If taking a mid-day break (e.g., gym, childcare), communicate availability to your team, 5) Consistent unavailability during core hours without manager approval may result in WFH privilege revocation.
rejected: You need to be online during work hours. Check with your manager about specifics.

prompt: What should I do if I witness workplace harassment?
chosen: If you witness or experience workplace harassment: 1) Document the incident(s) with date, time, location, people involved, and what was said/done, 2) Report to the HR Business Partner or use the anonymous Ethics Hotline (available 24/7), 3) The company has a zero-tolerance policy for harassment — all reports are investigated within 5 business days, 4) You are protected from retaliation for reporting in good faith, 5) The accused will be informed of the complaint and given opportunity to respond, 6) Investigation outcomes range from counseling to termination depending on severity, 7) If uncomfortable reporting to HR, you may approach any senior leader or the Ombudsperson. Retaliation against reporters is a separate violation and will result in disciplinary action.
rejected: Report it to HR. They'll handle it.

prompt: Can I accept gifts from clients or vendors?
chosen: Gift acceptance policy: 1) Gifts under $25 (meals, pens, small items) are acceptable without declaration, 2) Gifts valued $25-$100 must be declared to your manager and logged in the Compliance portal, 3) Gifts over $100 must be declined or returned — accepting them creates conflict of interest, 4) Cash gifts are NEVER acceptable regardless of amount, 5) Gifts from active vendors during contract negotiations must be declined entirely, 6) Holiday gifts (calendars, diaries) from vendors are acceptable if under $25, 7) Failure to declare gifts may result in disciplinary action.
