When in doubt, decline and report to the Compliance team.
rejected: Small gifts are fine. Don't accept expensive ones.

prompt: What is the company's policy on conflicts of interest?
chosen: Conflict of interest situations must be disclosed annually and when they arise: 1) Financial interests in competitors, vendors, or clients (owning >1% stock), 2) Outside employment or consulting work (including freelance), 3) Board positions or advisory roles in other organizations, 4) Family members working for competitors or vendors, 5) Personal relationships with direct reports or vendors you manage. Submit disclosure through the Compliance portal > Conflict of Interest. HR will assess and may require: divestment, recusal from decisions, or role adjustments. Undisclosed conflicts discovered later may result in termination. Annual disclosure is mandatory for all employees.
rejected: You should avoid conflicts of interest. Tell HR if you have one.

prompt: What documents do I need on my first day?
chosen: On your first day, bring: 1) Government-issued photo ID (passport, driver's license), 2) Social Security/Tax ID number documentation, 3) Signed offer letter and employment agreement, 4) Bank account details for salary deposit (voided check or bank letter), 5) Proof of address (utility bill, lease agreement), 6) Educational certificates (original for verification), 7) Previous employer's relieving letter and last 3 months' payslips, 8) Passport-size photographs (2 copies), 9) Completed tax forms (provided by HR), 10) Emergency contact information. If any documents are unavailable, inform HR before your start date. Incomplete documentation may delay payroll setup and benefits enrollment.
rejected: Bring your ID, bank details, and signed offer letter. HR will tell you everything else.

prompt: What is the exit interview process?
chosen: Exit interview process: 1) HR schedules a 30-minute exit interview during your final week, 2) You'll receive a confidential survey to complete before the meeting, 3) The interview covers: reasons for leaving, work experience, manager feedback, suggestions for improvement, 4) Participation is voluntary but encouraged — responses are anonymized in aggregate reports, 5) Exit interview feedback does not affect your rehire eligibility or final settlement, 6) You may request to skip the interview by informing HR, 7) All company property (laptop, badge, documents) must be returned before your final day, 8) Final settlement (including leave encashment) is processed within 30 days of separation.
rejected: HR will schedule an exit interview in your last week. It's optional.

prompt: Can I be rehired after leaving the company?
chosen: Rehire eligibility depends on separation circumstances: 1) Voluntary resignation with proper notice and good standing: Eligible for rehire after 12 months, 2) Layoff/restructuring: Eligible immediately with priority consideration, 3) Performance-based termination: Not eligible for rehire for 24 months, 4) Misconduct termination: Permanently ineligible, 5) Contract end: Eligible immediately. To apply for rehire: submit application through careers portal mentioning your previous employee ID and dates of employment. Previous managers are contacted for reference. Rehire candidates may negotiate compensation based on current market rates, not previous salary. Gaps in employment are not penalized.
rejected: It depends on why you left. Some people can come back, others can't.

prompt: Can I use my learning budget for conference attendance?
chosen: Yes, conference attendance is an approved use of your $2,000 annual learning budget. Guidelines: 1) Conference must be directly relevant to your role or career development, 2) Submit a 'Conference Request' through the LMS with: conference details, agenda, cost breakdown (registration, travel, accommodation), and business justification, 3) Manager approval required before booking, 4) Budget covers: registration fees, travel (economy class), accommodation (up to $200/night), and meals (per diem $50/day), 5) Post-conference, you must present key learnings to your team within 30 days, 6) If conference costs exceed $2,000, you may request a one-time budget extension with VP approval. Certification exams are also covered under learning budget.
rejected: Yes, conferences are covered. Get manager approval and submit expenses.

prompt: Does the company sponsor MBA or advanced degree programs?
chosen: The company offers partial sponsorship for advanced degrees (MBA, MS, specialized Master's) through the Executive Education Program: 1) Eligibility: 3+ years with company, 'Exceeds Expectations' rating in last review, manager recommendation, 2) Sponsorship covers up to 50% of tuition (maximum $10,000/year), 3) Program must be from an accredited institution and relevant to your career path at the company, 4) You must maintain a 'B' grade or higher, 5) Sponsorship requires a 2-year commitment post-graduation (if you leave before 2 years, you repay prorated amount), 6) Apply during Q1 through the LMS > Executive Education. Company also provides flexible schedules for class attendance. Full scholarships are competitive and limited to 10 employees per year.
rejected: The company might help with MBA costs. Ask HR about the program.

prompt: What mentoring programs are available?
chosen: The company offers three mentoring programs: 1) **New Hire Buddy** (first 90 days): Assigned peer mentor for onboarding, informal guidance, and culture integration, 2) **Career Mentoring** (6-month cycles): Senior leader mentor for career planning, skill development, and networking — apply through LMS > Mentoring Programs, 3) **Executive Sponsorship** (invitation only): VP-level sponsor for high-potential employees being groomed for leadership — includes quarterly 1:1s and visibility to senior leadership. All programs are voluntary and confidential. Mentors are trained and matched based on your development goals. You can participate in one program at a time. Mentoring does not guarantee promotion but provides valuable guidance and advocacy.
rejected: We have mentoring programs. Check the LMS for details.

prompt: Can I date someone who works in my department?
chosen: The company's Consensual Relationship Policy requires disclosure of romantic relationships between employees where one has direct or indirect authority over the other (manager-report, senior-junior in same chain of command). Requirements: 1) Both parties must disclose the relationship to HR within 30 days of it starting, 2) HR will assess reporting structure and may require: one party transferring to another team, removing supervisory authority, or implementing reporting adjustments, 3) Relationships between peers in the same department do not require disclosure but must not affect team dynamics, 4) Failure to disclose relationships that create conflicts may result in disciplinary action, 5) If relationship ends, inform HR to reverse any adjustments. The policy protects both employees and the company from favoritism claims.
rejected: Office relationships are okay as long as they don't affect work. Be professional.

prompt: What is the grievance procedure if I have a complaint about my manager?
chosen: Grievance procedure for manager-related complaints: 1) Attempt informal resolution by discussing directly with your manager (if comfortable), 2) If unresolved, escalate to your manager's supervisor or skip-level manager, 3) If still unresolved or uncomfortable with direct escalation, file a formal grievance with HR: submit written complaint with specific incidents, dates, and desired outcome, 4) HR investigates within 10 business days, interviewing you, your manager, and any witnesses, 5) HR presents findings and recommends resolution (mediation, coaching, role change, or disciplinary action), 6) You receive written outcome within 5 days of investigation completion, 7) You may appeal to the VP of HR within 15 days if unsatisfied. All grievance proceedings are confidential and protected from retaliation.
rejected: Talk to your manager first. If that doesn't work, go to HR.

prompt: Can I wear religious attire or observe religious practices at work?
chosen: The company fully supports religious expression and accommodation: 1) Religious attire (hijab, turban, kippah, cross, etc.) is permitted and protected under anti-discrimination policy, 2) Prayer/meditation breaks: You may take up to 30 minutes daily for religious observance (unpaid if exceeding standard break time), 3) Flexible scheduling for religious holidays: Request time off through the HR portal — these are separate from your casual leave balance (up to 3 days/year for religious observances not on the company holiday calendar), 4) Dietary accommodations: Company events provide options for religious dietary restrictions (halal, kosher, vegetarian), 5) If you experience discrimination or harassment related to religious practices, report to HR immediately. All accommodation requests are handled confidentially and without penalty.
rejected: Yes, religious practices are allowed. Just be respectful of others.

prompt: Can I install personal software on my company laptop?
chosen: Software installation policy: 1) Only company-approved software may be installed (list available on IT portal > Approved Software Catalog), 2) Personal software (games, social media apps, torrent clients, unlicensed tools) is strictly prohibited, 3) Productivity tools not on the approved list may be requested through IT > Software Request — IT evaluates for security, licensing, and compatibility, 4) Approved requests are installed by IT within 3 business days, 5) Unauthorized software discovered during security audits will be removed and may result in disciplinary action, 6) Open-source tools are evaluated case-by-case, 7) If you need specific software for your role, your manager can submit a 'Business Justification Request' for expedited approval. Personal use of company devices should be minimal.
rejected: Only install approved software. Ask IT if you need something specific.

prompt: What should I do if I suspect a security breach or phishing email?
chosen: If you suspect a security breach or receive a phishing email: 1) DO NOT click any links, download attachments, or reply to the email, 2) Forward the email to security@company.com with subject line 'SUSPECTED PHISHING,' 3) If you already clicked a link or entered credentials: immediately change your password, disconnect from the network, and call the IT Security Hotline (ext. 911), 4) If you notice unusual activity (files deleted, unauthorized access, strange pop-ups): disconnect from network and report to IT immediately, 5) The Security team investigates all reports within 2 hours, 6) You will not be penalized for reporting suspected breaches — quick reporting minimizes damage, 7) Regular security awareness training is mandatory (quarterly modules). Suspicious physical security (unknown persons in office) should be reported to Facilities.
rejected: Report it to IT immediately. Don't click anything suspicious.

prompt: Can I access company systems from a public computer (library, hotel)?
chosen: Accessing company systems from public computers is strongly discouraged but permitted with precautions: 1) Use only company-approved VPN to access internal systems, 2) Never save passwords on public computers — use private/incognito browser mode, 3) Do not download company data to the public computer, 4) Log out of all sessions when finished and clear browser history/cache, 5) Avoid accessing highly confidential data (HR records, financial data, client PII) on public computers, 6) If the computer is shared (library, internet cafe), ensure no one is shoulder-surfing, 7) Report any suspicious activity or potential compromise to IT Security immediately. Company-provided devices with VPN are always preferred for remote access.
rejected: You can use public computers but be careful. Use VPN and don't save passwords.

prompt: What is the company's policy on social media use?
chosen: Social media policy guidelines: 1) Personal accounts: You may identify yourself as an employee but must include 'opinions are my own' disclaimer, 2) Do not share confidential company information, unreleased product details, financial data, or client names, 3) Do not speak on behalf of the company unless authorized by Corporate Communications, 4) If posting about company events, achievements, or news, ensure information is already public, 5) Harassment, hate speech, or discriminatory content on personal accounts that reflects negatively on the company may result in disciplinary action, 6) Company social media accounts are managed by the Marketing team only, 7) Violations (sharing confidential info, misrepresenting company position) may result in termination. When in doubt, consult Corporate Communications before posting.
rejected: Be professional on social media. Don't share company secrets.

prompt: Can I bring my pet to the office?
chosen: Pet-friendly office policy: 1) Pets (dogs, cats only) are allowed on designated 'Pet Days' (every Friday) with prior registration, 2) Register your pet through the Facilities portal at least 24 hours in advance — there's a limit of 10 pets per floor per day, 3) Pets must be: vaccinated, house-trained, leashed in common areas, and non-aggressive, 4) Pet owners are responsible for cleanup and any damage, 5) Employees with allergies or phobias have priority — if your presence with a pet causes discomfort to a colleague, you'll be asked to make alternative arrangements, 6) Pets are not allowed in: cafeteria, meeting rooms, server rooms, or executive offices, 7) First-time incidents (pet causing disruption) result in warning; repeat incidents result in pet privilege revocation. Emotional support animals require separate accommodation approval through HR.
rejected: Pets are allowed on Fridays. Register your pet in advance.

prompt: What is the dress code for the office?
chosen: Office dress code policy: 1) **Standard days (Monday-Thursday)**: Business casual — collared shirts, blouses, slacks, skirts, dresses, closed-toe shoes. Prohibited: shorts, flip-flops, tank tops, ripped clothing, 2) **Casual Fridays**: Smart casual — jeans (no holes), clean sneakers, casual shirts, 3) **Client-facing days**: Business formal — suits, ties, formal dresses, leather shoes, 4) **Remote work days**: No dress code for video calls below waist level; professional attire visible on camera, 5) **Religious/cultural attire**: Fully supported and exempt from standard dress code, 6) **Safety-sensitive areas** (labs, server rooms): Closed-toe shoes and company-provided safety gear required regardless of dress code day. When in doubt, dress one level more formal. Managers may set team-specific standards if client interaction is frequent.
rejected: Business casual most days, casual Fridays. Dress up for client meetings.

prompt: Can I take unpaid leave for personal reasons?
chosen: Unpaid leave (Leave Without Pay - LWOP) is available for personal reasons when paid leave is exhausted or for extended absences: 1) Request must be submitted 30 days in advance through the HR portal, 2) Maximum duration: 90 days per year (cumulative), 3) During LWOP: no salary, no benefits accrual (health insurance continues for 30 days then converts to COBRA/self-pay), 4) Your position is not guaranteed upon return — company will make reasonable efforts to reinstate you in same/equivalent role, 5) LWOP counts as a break in service for vesting purposes (stock options, retirement), 6) Approval depends on: business needs, team coverage, your performance record, 7) Emergency LWOP (less than 30 days notice) requires VP approval. LWOP beyond 90 days is treated as a sabbatical or separation depending on circumstances.
rejected: You can take unpaid leave but it's not guaranteed. Ask HR.

prompt: What happens to my benefits if I'm laid off?
chosen: If laid off due to restructuring or downsizing: 1) **Severance pay**: 2 weeks per year of service (minimum 4 weeks), paid over standard payroll cycle, 2) **Health insurance**: Continues for 60 days post-separation, then COBRA/self-pay option available, 3) **Stock options**: Vested options can be exercised within 90 days; unvested options are forfeited, 4) **Leave encashment**: All unused earned leave is paid out at current daily rate, 5) **401k/PF**: Your contributions remain yours; employer contributions vest based on schedule, 6) **Outplacement support**: 3 months of career coaching, resume workshops, job search resources provided at company expense, 7) **Reference**: Company provides neutral confirmation of employment (dates, title) — managers may provide personal references separately, 8) You are eligible for rehire after 12 months. Severance package requires signing a release agreement.
rejected: You'll get severance pay and some benefits continuation. HR will explain everything.

prompt: Can I volunteer during work hours?
chosen: The company supports volunteerism through the Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) program: 1) **Volunteer Time Off (VTO)**: 16 hours/year (2 days) of paid time off for volunteering with approved non-profits, 2) Approved organizations must be registered 501(c)(3) charities (list on CSR portal), 3) VTO requests submitted through HR portal with: organization name, activity description, date, and impact statement, 4) Company also organizes quarterly group volunteer events (park cleanup, food bank, mentorship) — participation is voluntary but encouraged, 5) VTO cannot be accumulated or encashed — use it within the calendar year, 6) Volunteering for political campaigns or religious proselytizing is not covered under VTO, 7) Beyond 16 hours, use personal leave (casual/earned). Manager approval required but is typically granted for legitimate volunteer activities.
rejected: You get some volunteer days. Check with HR about approved organizations.

prompt: What is the policy on employee stock purchase plans (ESPP)?
chosen: The Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) allows you to buy company stock at a discount: 1) Eligibility: All full-time employees after 6 months of service, 2) Contribution: Up to 15% of salary deducted per payroll period (accumulated over 6-month offering period), 3) Purchase price: 85% of fair market value at the end of the offering period (15% discount), 4) Offering periods: January-June and July-December (enrollment opens 30 days before each period), 5) Maximum purchase: $25,000 worth of stock per year (IRS limit), 6) Enroll through the ESPP portal > Payroll Deduction Setup, 7) You can withdraw before purchase date (deductions refunded) but cannot re-enroll until next offering period, 8) Stock is deposited in your brokerage account within 5 days of purchase. Tax implications: discount is taxed as ordinary income; subsequent gains/losses are capital gains/losses. Consult a tax advisor.
rejected: You can buy company stock at a discount through payroll deduction. Check the ESPP portal.

prompt: Can I transfer to another department?
chosen: Internal transfer process: 1) Eligibility: 12+ months in current role, 'Meets Expectations' or higher rating, no active PIP, 2) Monitor internal job postings on the Careers portal (updated weekly), 3) Apply directly to open positions — your current manager is NOT notified until you reach the interview stage, 4) If selected: hiring manager coordinates with your current manager for transition timeline (typically 2-4 weeks), 5) If denied by current manager: escalation to HR Business Partner for mediation (manager must have business justification), 6) Compensation adjusts to the new role's salary band (may increase, decrease, or stay same), 7) Transfer does not reset your tenure — benefits, vesting, and PTO accrual continue uninterrupted, 8) You can apply for multiple roles but can only accept one transfer per year. Lateral transfers (same level) are more common than promotions through transfer.
rejected: You can apply for internal positions after a year. Your manager will know when you interview.

prompt: What is the company's policy on drug and alcohol use?
chosen: Drug and alcohol policy: 1) **Zero tolerance** for illegal drug use, possession, or distribution on company property or during work hours, 2) **Alcohol**: Not permitted during work hours except at company-sanctioned events (holiday parties, client dinners) where consumption must be moderate, 3) **Prescription medications**: Permitted but you must inform your manager if medication affects your ability to perform job safely (e.g., drowsiness), 4) **Testing**: Pre-employment drug screening is required for all new hires. Random testing is conducted for safety-sensitive roles (labs, driving). Post-incident testing follows workplace accidents, 5) **Violation consequences**: Immediate termination for illegal drugs; written warning for alcohol policy violations, 6) **Assistance**: Employees struggling with substance abuse may confidentially contact the Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for counseling and rehabilitation referrals before issues affect performance, 7) Being under the influence at work endangers safety and is grounds for immediate removal from premises.
rejected: No drugs or alcohol at work. Drug testing is required for new hires.

prompt: How do I request a reference letter for a loan or apartment?
chosen: Employment verification and reference letters: 1) Submit request through HR portal > Document Requests > Employment Verification, 2) Specify the purpose: loan application, apartment rental, visa application, etc., 3) Standard processing: 3-5 business days, 4) Letter includes: your employment dates, job title, and salary (if you authorize salary disclosure — required for most loans/apartments), 5) For detailed reference letters (performance, character): request must be approved by your current manager, 6) Urgent requests (24-48 hours): available with VP approval and documented deadline, 7) Letters are sent directly to the requesting institution (bank, landlord) or to you in a sealed envelope, 8) There is no fee for standard employment verification. Self-employed contractors must request verification through their agency contact.
rejected: Request employment verification through HR. It takes a few days.

prompt: What is the company's policy on workplace noise and distractions?
chosen: Workplace environment policy: 1) **Quiet hours**: 9 AM-12 PM and 2 PM-4 PM are designated focus hours — minimize non-urgent conversations, use chat instead of walking to desks, 2) **Meeting rooms**: Use for calls longer than 10 minutes; don't hold conversations in hallways near workspaces, 3) **Headphones**: Permitted and encouraged for focus work; if someone is wearing headphones, send a message instead of interrupting, 4) **Shared spaces**: Keep volume low in break rooms, cafeterias; clean up after yourself, 5) **Music**: Personal music is allowed with headphones only; no speakers in open office areas, 6) **Construction/facilities work**: Scheduled outside quiet hours when possible; advance notice provided for unavoidable disruptions, 7) If noise consistently affects your productivity: discuss with your manager, request a desk relocation, or book a quiet room. Repeated policy violations (loud calls, disruptive behavior) may result in HR intervention.
rejected: Keep noise down during work hours. Use meeting rooms for calls.

prompt: Can I get a copy of all the personal data the company has on me?
chosen: You have the right to access your personal data under data privacy laws (GDPR, CCPA, etc.): 1) Submit a 'Data Access Request' through the Privacy portal or email privacy@company.com, 2) The company will provide within 30 days: employment records, performance reviews, compensation history, benefits enrollment, attendance records, training records, communications (HR-related), 3) Data is provided in a secure, encrypted digital format, 4) You may request correction of inaccurate data by submitting supporting documentation, 5) You may request deletion of non-essential data (but employment records are legally required to be retained for 7 years), 6) Third-party data (background checks, insurance claims) is provided by the respective vendors, 7) If you suspect unauthorized use of your data, report to the Privacy Officer immediately. Requests are handled confidentially by the Legal/Compliance team. You may make one comprehensive request per year at no cost.
rejected: You can request your data from HR. They'll provide what they have on file.

prompt: What happens if I accidentally share confidential information?
chosen: If you accidentally share confidential information: 1) Immediately notify your manager and the Information Security team (security@company.com), 2) Specify: what was shared, with whom, how (email, chat, verbal), and when, 3) Do NOT attempt to recall/delete the information yourself — let Security handle remediation, 4) Security will assess impact: was it internal (another employee) or external (client, competitor, public), 5) Remediation may include: recalling emails, requesting recipient deletion, legal notices, or notifying affected parties, 6) Accidental disclosures are investigated to determine if it was genuine error or negligence, 7) First-time accidental disclosures typically result in coaching and retraining; repeated incidents may result in disciplinary action, 8) The company has legal obligations to report certain breaches (client PII, financial data) to regulators — prompt reporting minimizes legal exposure. Never hide an accidental disclosure.
rejected: Report it to IT immediately. They'll figure out what to do.

prompt: What is the company's policy on jury duty?
chosen: Jury duty is a civic obligation the company fully supports: 1) You receive your regular salary during jury duty (up to 15 working days), 2) Submit jury summons documentation to HR within 5 days of receipt, 3) The company pays the difference between court compensation and your regular salary, 4) Beyond 15 days, you may use accrued leave or take unpaid leave, 5) You're expected to work your regular shift on days when court is not in session (e.g., selected but not serving, weekend adjournments), 6) Jury duty time is not deducted from your leave balance, 7) Failure to report for jury duty when summoned may have legal consequences — inform your manager immediately upon receiving summons. Court attendance certificates may be required for payroll processing.
rejected: You get paid for jury duty. Just show HR your summons.

prompt: Can I take leave for my spouse's childbirth?
chosen: Parental leave policy: 1) **Primary caregiver** (birth mother): 12 weeks maternity leave (can start 2 weeks before due date), 2) **Secondary caregiver** (father/non-birth parent): 4 weeks paternity leave within 6 months of birth/adoption, 3) **Adoption leave**: Same as biological parents — 12 weeks primary, 4 weeks secondary (within 6 months of placement), 4) Leave is paid at 100% salary for first 8 weeks (primary) or 2 weeks (secondary), then 60% for remaining period, 5) You may use accrued earned leave to top up the 60% period to 100%, 6) Benefits (health insurance, retirement) continue during parental leave, 7) You may extend parental leave by up to 4 additional weeks using earned leave or unpaid leave, 8) Upon return, you're guaranteed same or equivalent position. Notify HR and your manager as soon as pregnancy/adoption is confirmed to plan coverage.

prompt: What is the bereavement leave policy?
chosen: Bereavement leave provides time off for mourning and funeral arrangements: 1) **Immediate family** (spouse, parent, child, sibling): 5 working days paid leave, 2) **Extended family** (grandparent, in-law, aunt/uncle): 3 working days paid leave, 3) **Close friend**: 1 working day paid leave (manager discretion), 4) Bereavement leave is separate from other leave types and does not reduce your leave balance, 5) If additional time is needed, you may use earned leave or request unpaid leave, 6) Travel time for out-of-state/international funerals: up to 2 additional days (unpaid unless using accrued leave), 7) Grief counseling is available through the Employee Assistance Program (EAP) — up to 6 free sessions, 8) Notify your manager as soon as possible; HR documentation (obituary, funeral program) may be requested for records. prompt: Can I work reduced hours (part-time) temporarily?

This is distinct from permanent part-time employment (which requires role reclassification).

prompt: What is the company's policy on military leave?
chosen: Military leave is protected under USERRA (Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act): 1) **Duration**: Up to 5 years cumulative (per employer) for active duty, training, or deployment, 2) **Notification**: Provide advance notice when possible (verbal or written), except for emergencies, 3) **Pay**: Unpaid during military leave, but you may use accrued leave to receive pay, 4) **Benefits**: Health insurance continues for up to 24 months (you pay full premium if leave exceeds 30 days), 5) **Retirement**: Military service counts as continuous service for vesting purposes, 6) **Reemployment**: Guaranteed same or equivalent position upon return (with some exceptions for changed circumstances), 7) **Training**: You're entitled to time off for annual training/reserve duty (typically 2 weeks/year) — use military leave or accrued PTO, 8) Upon return, you're entitled to catch-up contributions for retirement plans. The company supports military employees and complies fully with USERRA protections.
rejected: Military leave is protected by law. You can take up to 5 years and return to your job.

prompt: How do I report a workplace injury?

Failure to report within 24 hours may delay workers' comp benefits. Near-misses (no injury but hazardous situation) should also be reported to prevent future incidents.
rejected: Tell your manager right away and fill out an incident report. Workers' comp will cover medical costs.

prompt: Can I use company resources for my side business?
chosen: Company resources may NOT be used for personal business activities: 1) Prohibited: Company laptop, phone, email, software licenses, office supplies, printers, meeting rooms, or company time for your side business, 2) Permitted: Using personal devices on your own time (breaks, before/after work) for personal business, 3) Conflict of interest: If your side business competes with the company, serves company clients, or uses company knowledge/trade secrets, you must disclose it to HR and may be required to cease operations, 4) Intellectual property: Anything created on company time or using company resources belongs to the company, 5) Moonlighting: Side business is permitted if it doesn't interfere with job performance, create conflicts, or use company resources, 6) Violations may result in disciplinary action up to termination. If uncertain whether an activity is permitted, consult HR before proceeding.

prompt: What is the policy on employee discounts or partnerships?
chosen: The company negotiates employee discounts with various vendors: 1) Available discounts: Cell phone plans, gym memberships, software licenses, travel bookings, car purchases, retail stores, 2) Access discounts through the Benefits portal > Employee Perks > Partner Discounts, 3) Discounts are for personal use only — reselling or purchasing for others is prohibited, 4) Some vendors require employment verification (company email or badge), 5) Discounts vary by vendor and may change — check portal for current offers, 6) The company does not endorse or guarantee vendor products/services — use at your own discretion, 7) If a vendor provides poor service, report to HR (the partnership may be reviewed), 8) New discount partnerships are negotiated annually — suggest vendors through the Benefits portal. Contractors and part-time employees may have access to select discounts (noted in portal).

prompt: Can I bring a complaint against a coworker?
chosen: Filing a complaint against a coworker: 1) **Informal resolution**: If comfortable, discuss the issue directly with the coworker first (many conflicts resolve through communication), 2) **Formal complaint**: Submit written complaint to your HR Business Partner or through the Ethics Hotline (anonymous option available), 3) Include: specific incidents, dates, witnesses, impact on your work, and desired outcome, 4) **Investigation**: HR investigates within 10 business days — interviews you, the coworker, and witnesses separately, 5) **Confidentiality**: Complaint details are shared only with those necessary for the investigation, 6) **Outcome**: HR determines if policy was violated and recommends resolution (mediation, coaching, written warning, suspension, or termination), 7) You receive written summary of outcome (specific disciplinary actions are confidential), 8) **Retaliation**: Protected — the coworker cannot retaliate against you for filing a complaint in good faith. False or malicious complaints may result in disciplinary action against the complainant.

prompt: What happens if the company closes my office location?
chosen: Office closure/relocation policy: 1) **Notice**: Company provides minimum 60 days advance notice (or as required by WARN Act for large closures), 2) **Relocation options**: You may be offered transfer to another company office (with relocation assistance if moving is required), 3) **Remote work**: If your role allows, you may transition to full remote work (with equipment and internet subsidy), 4) **Severance**: If no suitable alternative is available or you decline relocation, you receive severance: 2 weeks per year of service (minimum 4 weeks), plus COBRA health insurance continuation, 5) **Outplacement**: 3 months of career coaching and job search support, 6) **Accrued benefits**: All unused leave is paid out; vested stock options can be exercised per standard timeline, 7) **Unemployment**: You're eligible for unemployment benefits (company does not contest legitimate layoff claims), 8) The company prioritizes finding alternative employment for affected employees and may share openings with partner organizations.

prompt: Can I take a leave of absence for mental health reasons?
chosen: Mental health leave is treated with the same importance as physical health: 1) **Short-term**: Use sick leave or short-term disability (up to 90 days) for mental health treatment (therapy, inpatient care, burnout recovery), 2) **Long-term**: Extended mental health leave (90 days to 6 months) available through long-term disability insurance, 3) **Documentation**: Requires certification from a licensed mental health professional (therapist, psychiatrist, psychologist), 4) **Confidentiality**: Medical details are kept separate from employment records and shared only with HR's medical reviewer (not your manager), 5) **Benefits**: Health insurance continues during approved medical leave; you continue paying your portion, 6) **Return to work**: Gradual return (part-time for 2 weeks) may be arranged with manager approval, 7) **EAP**: Employee Assistance Program provides up to 6 free counseling sessions — available before leave is necessary, 8) **Protected**: Mental health leave is protected under FMLA/ADA — your position is held for you, and you cannot be penalized for taking approved medical leave. Stigma around mental health is not tolerated.

prompt: What is the policy on employee surveillance or monitoring?
chosen: Employee monitoring policy (transparency and privacy balance): 1) **What is monitored**: Company email, network activity, laptop usage, application usage, time spent on websites, company phone calls (not personal calls), badge swipes, security cameras, 2) **What is NOT monitored**: Personal email accounts, personal phone calls, personal devices (unless connected to company network), off-duty activities, social media (unless it violates company policy), 3) **Purpose**: Security, productivity assessment, policy compliance, investigation of misconduct, 4) **Consent**: By using company resources, you consent to monitoring (stated in employment agreement and IT policy), 5) **Access**: Monitoring data is accessed only by: IT Security (security incidents), HR (policy violations), Legal (investigations), 6) **Retention**: Monitoring data is retained for 1 year (unless part of active investigation), 7) **Your rights**: You may request access to your monitoring data through Privacy portal, 8) **Limitations**: Monitoring is not continuous real-time surveillance — it's used for specific purposes (security, investigations, aggregated productivity reports). Personal use of company resources should be minimal and reasonable.
rejected: The company monitors your work devices and network activity. Don't do personal stuff on them.

prompt: Can I negotiate my salary after the annual review?
chosen: Salary negotiation outside the annual review cycle: 1) **Standard timing**: Salary adjustments occur during annual review cycle (effective April 1st), 2) **Off-cycle increases**: Permitted in specific circumstances: promotion, significant scope expansion, counter-offer (competing job offer), market adjustment (salary significantly below market), retention risk (high performer likely to leave), 3) **Process**: Schedule discussion with your manager — present: market data (salary surveys, Glassdoor, Payscale), your contributions, increased responsibilities, or competing offer, 4) **Manager approval**: Manager submits justification to HR and Compensation team, 5) **Timeline**: Off-cycle reviews take 4-6 weeks for approval, 6) **Success rate**: Approximately 30% of off-cycle requests are approved (varies by business unit and budget), 7) **Alternatives**: If salary increase is not approved, discuss: one-time bonus, additional PTO, professional development budget, flexible schedule, title change, 8) **Frequency**: Only one off-cycle salary review per year. The company aims to pay competitively but budget constraints apply.

prompt: What is the company's policy on political activities?
chosen: Political activity policy: 1) **Personal activities**: You may engage in political activities on personal time (volunteering for campaigns, attending rallies, posting on social media), 2) **Company resources**: Cannot be used for political activities (email, printers, meeting rooms, company time), 3) **Company position**: The company does not endorse political candidates or parties (except on issues directly affecting business, communicated by Corporate Communications), 4) **Solicitation**: No political solicitation in the workplace (asking coworkers for donations, distributing campaign materials), 5) **Diversity of views**: Political discussions at work should be respectful; harassment or discrimination based on political beliefs is prohibited, 6) **Running for office**: If running for elected office, you must use personal leave for campaign activities; if elected, you may need to take leave of absence or resign (depending on the role and conflicts), 7) **Lobbying**: Company lobbyists represent company interests only — employees cannot lobby for personal political causes using company resources, 8) **Election day**: You may use up to 2 hours of paid time to vote if polls are not open before/after your shift. prompt: Can I get reimbursed for professional association memberships?

If you leave the company, you're not required to reimburse membership costs (they're considered a benefit, not an advance).

prompt: What is the policy on workplace romances between peers?

If uncertain whether your situation requires disclosure, consult HR confidentially.

prompt: Can I take leave for a natural disaster or emergency?

prompt: What is the policy on employees serving on nonprofit boards?

Board service should not interfere with job performance or create conflicts of interest.

prompt: What is the policy on employees filing patents or inventions?
chosen: Intellectual property and invention policy: 1) **Company-owned IP**: Inventions, patents, or innovations created using company resources, during work hours, or related to company business belong to the company, 2) **Disclosure**: Submit invention disclosure to the Legal team within 30 days of creation, 3) **Filing**: Company decides whether to file patent (covers all costs) — you're listed as inventor, 4) **Compensation**: If patent generates revenue, inventor receives 10% of net licensing revenue for life of patent, 5) **Personal inventions**: Created entirely on your own time, without company resources, unrelated to company business — belong to you (but must be disclosed to confirm no conflict), 6) **Academic publications**: If research leads to publications, company retains IP rights but grants you permission to publish with Legal review, 7) **Post-employment**: IP created during employment remains company property after you leave, 8) Violations (concealing inventions, using company IP for personal gain) may result in termination and legal action. The company encourages innovation and supports inventors.

prompt: Can I take a sabbatical for travel or personal projects?

prompt: What is the company's policy on employees receiving awards or recognition?

prompt: Can I bring a service animal to the office?

If you have concerns about a service animal, contact HR confidentially.

prompt: What is the policy on employees investing in startups or side ventures?

prompt: Can I request a copy of my employment contract?

If you have questions about contract terms, schedule a meeting with HR.

prompt: What is the policy on workplace celebrations and events?
chosen: Workplace celebrations and social events policy: 1) **Company-sponsored**: Holiday party, team-building events, milestone celebrations (work anniversaries, project completions) — organized by HR/Corporate Events, attendance is voluntary but encouraged, 2) **Team celebrations**: Small celebrations (birthdays, baby showers, retirements) are permitted — use break room, keep within 30 minutes, clean up afterward, 3) **Alcohol**: Company events may serve alcohol — consumption must be moderate; excessive drinking or intoxication at company events violates policy and may result in disciplinary action, 4) **Collections**: Voluntary collections (gifts, cards) are permitted but cannot be mandatory or create pressure — no manager-led collections for direct reports, 5) **Inclusivity**: Celebrations should be inclusive and respectful of diverse backgrounds; avoid assumptions about religious/cultural practices, 6) **Budget**: Team celebration budget: $200/quarter per team (submitted through manager for reimbursement), 7) **After-hours**: Social gatherings outside work hours are not company-sponsored — attendance does not count as work time, injuries are not covered by workers' comp, 8) The company encourages positive team culture while maintaining professional standards.

prompt: Can I work while on short-term disability leave?
chosen: Working during disability leave policy: 1) **Short-term disability (STD)**: Generally, you should NOT work while on STD leave — the leave is for medical recovery and working may invalidate your claim, 2) **Exceptions**: Light-duty or part-time work may be permitted if: your doctor approves in writing, the work does not conflict with your medical restrictions, HR approves the arrangement, 3) **Impact on benefits**: Working while on STD may reduce or eliminate disability payments (varies by insurance policy), 4) **Communication**: If you feel well enough to work before your scheduled return, contact HR and your doctor — early return requires medical clearance, 5) **Remote work**: Working from home while on STD is still considered work and requires the same approvals, 6) **Volunteer work**: Not permitted during STD leave (may be viewed as ability to work), 7) **Side business**: Operating a business while on STD may be investigated as fraud by the insurance company, 8) **Long-term disability (LTD)**: Stricter rules — any work income may reduce LTD benefits. Working while on disability leave without approval may result in claim denial, benefit repayment demands, and disciplinary action. Always consult HR and your doctor before any work activity during disability leave.

prompt: What is the company's policy on employee feedback or suggestion programs?

prompt: Can I transfer my retirement account to a different provider?

Consult a financial advisor before making retirement account changes — there may be tax implications.

prompt: What is the policy on employees using AI tools for work?

prompt: Can I request ergonomic equipment for my home office?

prompt: What is the policy on employees participating in market research or surveys?
chosen: Market research and survey participation policy: 1) **External surveys**: You may participate in industry surveys, academic research, or market studies on personal time — no disclosure required, 2) **Company-sponsored surveys**: Participation is voluntary unless stated as mandatory (e.g., annual engagement survey), 3) **Compensation**: You may keep compensation from external surveys (gift cards, cash) unless survey was conducted during work hours, 4) **Confidentiality**: Cannot share company-specific data, strategies, or client information in external surveys — respond in general terms or decline, 5) **Competitor surveys**: If invited to participate in competitor's market research, decline and report to Corporate Strategy team (may indicate competitor intelligence gathering), 6) **Using company name**: If survey asks for employer name, you may state the company name but clarify that opinions are your own, 7) **Work time**: Participating in external surveys during work hours requires manager approval and use of accrued leave, 8) **Academic research**: If research involves company data or employees, researcher must sign confidentiality agreement and obtain IRB approval. prompt: Can I get advance payment for my salary?
chosen: Salary advance policy: 1) **Eligibility**: Full-time employees with 6+ months of service, no outstanding salary advances, 2) **Maximum advance**: 50% of one month's net salary (after deductions), 3) **Repayment**: Deducted from next 2 payroll cycles (50% from each), 4) **Reasons**: Medical emergencies, natural disasters, unexpected housing costs, critical family needs — salary advance is not for routine expenses or discretionary purchases, 5) **Application**: Submit Salary Advance Request through HR portal with: amount needed, reason, repayment plan, and supporting documentation (bills, medical invoices), 6) **Approval**: HR reviews within 3 business days — approval depends on financial hardship severity and repayment ability, 7) **Frequency**: Maximum 2 salary advances per calendar year, 8) **Interest**: No interest charged (company benefit), 9) **Separation**: If you leave before repayment is complete, outstanding balance is deducted from final settlement. Salary advance is an emergency benefit — frequent requests may trigger financial counseling referral through EAP. Alternative: Employee Relief Fund (grants, not loans) for severe hardship.

prompt: What is the company's policy on employees running for public office?
chosen: Public office candidacy policy: 1) **Local offices** (school board, city council, county commissioner): Permitted with approval — submit request to HR with: office sought, campaign timeline, how you'll manage work responsibilities, 2) **State/federal offices**: Require leave of absence upon becoming a candidate (cannot simultaneously hold company position and campaign for high office), 3) **Campaign activities**: Must occur outside work hours; cannot use company resources (email, phone, office, staff) for campaign, 4) **Company endorsement**: The company does not endorse candidates (including employees running for office) — your candidacy is personal, 5) **Conflicts**: If elected office creates conflict with company interests (regulatory, competitive), HR will assess and may require role adjustment or resignation, 6) **Media**: If asked about your employer in campaign materials/interviews, you may state your employment but clarify that the company does not endorse your candidacy, 7) **Return to work**: After election (won or lost), you may return to your position if you took leave — if you won, resignation is required, 8) **Legal compliance**: Campaign finance laws, ethics rules, and company policies all apply — consult Legal before announcing candidacy. The company respects civic engagement but prioritizes avoiding conflicts of interest.

prompt: What is the policy on employees accepting job offers from competitors?
chosen: Moving to a competitor policy: 1) **Non-compete clause**: If your employment agreement includes a non-compete (typically Senior Manager+ or roles with trade secret access), you cannot join a direct competitor for 3-6 months after separation — duration and scope are defined in your contract, 2) **Non-solicitation**: All employees are bound by 12-month non-solicitation (cannot recruit company employees or clients after leaving), 3) **Company property**: Return all company property (laptop, documents, badges, data) before your last day — retaining company property may result in legal action, 4) **Exit interview**: Standard process — you're not required to disclose your next employer but may voluntarily share for alumni network, 5) **Outstanding obligations**: Repay any outstanding advances, training bonds, or relocation agreements per contract terms, 6) **Reference**: Company provides neutral employment verification; future employer may contact you directly for reference, 7) **Legal review**: If non-compete applies, Legal team will send reminder letter outlining restrictions — violation may result in injunction and damages, 8) **Garden leave**: In rare cases, company may place you on paid leave during notice period (if you have access to sensitive information about ongoing deals). The company respects career mobility while protecting legitimate business interests.
rejected: You can join competitors but check your non-compete agreement first.

prompt: Can I use my employee discount for family members?
chosen: Employee discount sharing policy: 1) **Immediate family** (spouse, children, parents living in same household): May use your employee discount with your explicit permission — they must present your employee ID or verification letter, 2) **Friends/extended family**: Not permitted — discounts are for employee and immediate household only, 3) **Online purchases**: Use your company email for verification — sharing login credentials violates IT policy, 4) **Resale**: Purchasing items with employee discount for resale is prohibited and may result in discount privilege revocation and disciplinary action, 5) **Limits**: Some vendors limit discount usage (e.g., 2 transactions/month per employee) — check specific vendor terms, 6) **Abuse**: Excessive or suspicious discount usage may be audited — maintain records of family purchases, 7) **Partner changes**: If a vendor changes discount terms or ends partnership, you'll receive 30 days notice — no grandfathering, 8) **Contractors/part-time**: May have limited or no discount access (varies by vendor — noted in Benefits portal). Employee discounts are a benefit, not a right — abuse may result in loss of privileges.
rejected: Family members can use your discount. Don't share with friends.

prompt: What is the policy on workplace bullying (not harassment)?
chosen: Workplace bullying policy (distinct from illegal harassment): 1) **Definition**: Repeated unreasonable behavior intended to intimidate, degrade, humiliate, or undermine an employee (yelling, exclusion, sabotage, constant criticism, unreasonable deadlines), 2) **Reporting**: Report to HR Business Partner or through Ethics Hotline — bullying may not be illegal but violates company values, 3) **Investigation**: HR investigates within 10 business days — interviews victim, alleged bully, and witnesses, 4) **Resolution**: If bullying is confirmed: coaching, written warning, mandatory training, role transfer, or termination (depending on severity and history), 5) **Support**: Bullying victims may access EAP counseling (up to 10 sessions), 6) **Retaliation**: Protected — the bully cannot retaliate against the reporter, 7) **Difference from harassment**: Harassment is based on protected characteristics (race, gender, religion) and is illegal; bullying may be based on personality conflict or power dynamics but still violates policy, 8) **Prevention**: Annual training on respectful workplace behavior — managers are held to higher standards. The company maintains a zero-tolerance policy for bullying. Repeated bullying behavior results in progressive discipline.
rejected: Bullying is not acceptable. Report it to HR.

prompt: Can I take leave for religious pilgrimages or ceremonies?
chosen: Religious observance and pilgrimage policy: 1) **Standard religious holidays**: Up to 3 days/year for religious observances not on the company holiday calendar — paid leave, separate from casual leave balance, 2) **Extended religious leave** (pilgrimages, extended ceremonies): Use accrued earned leave or request unpaid leave — duration varies (1 week to 1 month), 3) **Major pilgrimages** (Hajj, Kumbh Mela, Vatican visits): Sabbatical or extended unpaid leave may be arranged — discuss with HR 6 months in advance for planning, 4) **Flexible scheduling**: You may adjust work hours to accommodate daily prayer, Sabbath observance, or religious study — coordinate with manager, 5) **Prayer/meditation space**: Multi-faith prayer room available in all offices (locations on Facilities portal) — open to all employees, 6) **Dietary**: Religious dietary accommodations at company events (halal, kosher, vegetarian, vegan) — request when RSVPing, 7) **Attire**: Religious attire is fully protected and encouraged — no dress code restrictions apply, 8) **No discrimination**: Requests for religious accommodation are approved without penalty; denial of religious accommodation is prohibited under Title VII. The company respects diverse religious practices and provides reasonable accommodations.

prompt: What is the company's policy on employee podcasts or YouTube channels?
chosen: Employee content creation (podcasts, YouTube, blogs) policy: 1) **Personal content**: You may create podcasts, videos, or blogs on personal time about personal interests — no disclosure required, 2) **Work-related content**: If content discusses your role, industry expertise, or work experiences: disclose to Corporate Communications, ensure no confidential information is shared, clarify that opinions are your own, 3) **Company resources**: Cannot use company equipment, office space, or work time for content creation, 4) **Monetization**: Revenue from personal content is yours — company has no claim, 5) **Company name/logo**: Cannot use company branding in your content without written permission from Corporate Communications, 6) **Conflicts**: Content that criticizes the company, reveals trade secrets, harasses coworkers, or creates reputational harm may result in disciplinary action, 7) **Speaking fees**: If invited to speak or create content because of your company role, fees are yours to keep but must not conflict with job duties, 8) **Approval process**: Submit content plan to Corporate Communications (if work-related) — approval takes 5 business days. The company encourages thought leadership while managing reputational risk.
rejected: You can create personal content. Just don't share company secrets or use company resources.

prompt: Can I request a letter of recommendation from the company?
chosen: Recommendation letter policy: 1) **Current employees**: Request through HR portal > Document Requests > Recommendation Letter — your manager writes the letter, HR reviews for consistency, 2) **Former employees**: Contact your former manager directly — if unavailable, HR provides standard employment verification only (dates, title), 3) **Content**: Letters typically include: employment dates, role responsibilities, key achievements, skills, and overall performance assessment, 4) **Purpose**: Specify purpose (graduate school, new job, professional certification, immigration) — letter may be tailored accordingly, 5) **Timeline**: 5-7 business days for standard requests; urgent requests (48 hours) require VP approval, 6) **Format**: Letters are on company letterhead, signed by manager or HR, delivered digitally (PDF) or in sealed envelope, 7) **Limitations**: Company does not write recommendation letters for: legal proceedings, immigration cases requiring special certifications, character references for criminal matters, 8) **Negative performance**: If performance was below expectations, the letter will be neutral (factual employment details only) — you may request your manager write a personal letter separately. Recommendation letters are provided as a professional courtesy.
rejected: You can request a recommendation letter through HR. Your manager will write it.

prompt: What is the policy on employees sharing salary information with coworkers?
chosen: Salary transparency and discussion policy: 1) **Your right**: Under the National Labor Relations Act (NLRA), you have the legal right to discuss your salary with coworkers — the company cannot prohibit or penalize salary discussions, 2) **Company stance**: While legal, the company encourages focusing on your own compensation and career growth rather than comparing with peers (compensation varies based on role, experience, performance, market factors), 3) **Manager guidance**: Managers should not discourage salary discussions but may redirect to individual career development conversations, 4) **Pay equity**: The company conducts annual pay equity audits to ensure fair compensation across gender, race, and other protected characteristics — results are shared in aggregate, 5) **Salary bands**: Job postings include salary ranges; employees can request their role's salary band from HR, 6) **Confidentiality**: While you can discuss your own salary, accessing other employees' compensation data (through HR systems, payroll) without authorization is prohibited and may result in termination, 7) **Retaliation**: Managers cannot retaliate against employees for discussing compensation — report violations to HR immediately, 8) **Benefits**: Health insurance costs, retirement contributions are similarly protected for discussion. The company supports transparency while maintaining individual privacy.
rejected: You can discuss your salary with coworkers — it's your legal right.

prompt: Can I work from a coworking space instead of home or office?
chosen: Coworking space work policy: 1) **Eligibility**: Approved for employees with remote work arrangements who prefer coworking spaces over home office, 2) **Reimbursement**: Up to $300/month for coworking space membership (must be a legitimate business with security, internet, workspace), 3) **Approval**: Submit coworking space details through Facilities portal > Alternative Workspace with: location, monthly cost, amenities, and manager approval, 4) **Security**: Coworking space must meet company security standards: private phone booths for confidential calls, secure internet (no public Wi-Fi), locked storage for company equipment, 5) **Attendance**: Mark attendance as 'Remote Work' — coworking space address is logged for emergency contact purposes, 6) **Equipment**: Standard remote work equipment applies (laptop, monitor reimbursement) — coworking space does not provide additional equipment, 7) **Tax implications**: Coworking space reimbursement is non-taxable (considered business expense), 8) **Availability**: Subject to annual remote work budget — if budget is exhausted, requests are waitlisted. Coworking spaces are a valid alternative to home office for employees seeking professional environment without commuting to main office.

prompt: What is the policy on employees accepting bribes or kickbacks?
chosen: Anti-bribery and anti-kickback policy (zero tolerance): 1) **Definition**: Bribes include money, gifts, favors, employment offers, or anything of value offered to influence business decisions; kickbacks are payments received for directing business to a vendor, 2) **Prohibition**: Absolutely no employee may offer, accept, or solicit bribes or kickbacks — this is illegal under the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act (FCPA) and local laws, 3) **Vendor interactions**: If a vendor offers gifts beyond nominal value (over $100), decline and report to Compliance immediately, 4) **International business**: Same standards apply globally — no 'facilitation payments' (small bribes to speed up routine actions) are permitted, 5) **Reporting**: Report suspected bribery to the Ethics Hotline (anonymous), Compliance team, or Legal — all reports are investigated within 48 hours, 6) **Consequences**: Violations result in immediate termination, possible criminal prosecution, and civil penalties (fines up to $1M+ for individuals), 7) **Due diligence**: Vendors are screened for corruption history before engagement, 8) **Training**: Annual anti-bribery training is mandatory for all employees, especially those in procurement, sales, and international roles. There are NO exceptions to the anti-bribery policy. When in doubt, decline and report.
rejected: Bribes and kickbacks are illegal and will get you fired. Don't do it.

prompt: Can I take leave to care for an elderly parent or family member?
chosen: Family caregiver leave policy: 1) **Short-term care**: Use accrued leave (casual, sick, earned) for short-term family care needs (doctor appointments, illness, surgery recovery), 2) **FMLA leave**: Up to 12 weeks unpaid, job-protected leave to care for spouse, child, or parent with serious health condition — eligibility: 12+ months with company, 1,250+ hours worked, 3) **Flexible work**: If ongoing care is needed, discuss flexible schedule, reduced hours, or remote work arrangement with manager (case-by-case approval), 4) **Elder care resources**: Company partners with elder care services to provide: referrals to care facilities, legal/financial consultation, support groups — access through Benefits portal > Family Care, 5) **Emergency care**: If family member has sudden health crisis, notify manager immediately — emergency leave is granted while you arrange longer-term solution, 6) **Long-term care**: Beyond FMLA, you may request unpaid leave of absence (up to 3 months) or explore sabbatical option, 7) **Documentation**: FMLA requires medical certification from healthcare provider — HR provides forms, 8) **Return to work**: FMLA guarantees same or equivalent position; job is protected. Caring for family is important — the company provides resources and flexibility to support caregivers.

prompt: What is the company's policy on employees filing lawsuits or legal claims?
chosen: Employee legal claims policy: 1) **Workplace disputes**: Attempt internal resolution first (HR, grievance procedure, mediation) before pursuing legal action — many disputes are resolved internally, 2) **Legal representation**: You may consult an attorney at any time — company does not prohibit legal consultation, 3) **Arbitration clause**: Most employment agreements include mandatory arbitration (instead of court) for employment disputes — check your agreement, 4) **Whistleblower claims**: If reporting illegal activity (fraud, safety violations, discrimination), you're protected under whistleblower laws — company cannot retaliate, 5) **Workers' compensation**: Workplace injury claims are handled through workers' comp system (no right to sue employer for workplace injuries except in extreme cases), 6) **Class action**: Participation in class action lawsuits against the company may affect employment status — consult Legal, 7) **Company support**: If you're sued for actions taken within scope of employment (e.g., client sues you for work product), company provides legal defense at company expense, 8) **Confidentiality**: Legal proceedings may require disclosure of confidential information — coordinate with company Legal team. The company prefers resolving disputes through internal processes but respects employees' legal rights.
rejected: You can file legal claims but try internal resolution first. Check your employment agreement.

prompt: Can I get a company phone or tablet?
chosen: Company device policy: 1) **Eligibility**: Laptops are standard for all employees; phones/tablets are provided based on role need (frequent travel, client-facing, after-hours availability, field work), 2) **Request process**: Submit device request through IT portal > Mobile Devices with: business justification, manager approval, and device type (phone, tablet, both), 3) **Approval criteria**: IT and manager assess: frequency of mobile work, client communication needs, security requirements, budget, 4) **Personal use**: Limited personal use is permitted on company devices (calls, texts, apps) — expect no privacy on company devices, 5) **Cost**: Company covers: device cost, data plan, insurance — employee responsible for excessive personal charges (international calls, premium apps), 6) **Return**: Device must be returned upon separation or if role changes and device is no longer needed, 7) **Loss/damage**: Report lost/stolen devices to IT immediately — company covers replacement; negligence (leaving in public) may result in deductible charge, 8) **BYOD alternative**: If personal device is used for work, company reimburses $50/month and installs mobile device management (MDM) software for security. Not all employees qualify for company phones — justify business need for approval.

prompt: What is the policy on employees using company email for personal communications?
chosen: Company email usage policy: 1) **Primary purpose**: Company email is for business communications — personal use should be minimal, occasional, and appropriate (e.g., urgent family matters), 2) **Privacy**: No expectation of privacy — company may monitor, access, or disclose email content for business, security, or legal purposes, 3) **Prohibited**: Personal email accounts (Gmail, Yahoo) cannot be accessed through company email system; mass personal emails (invitations, fundraisers, political campaigns) are prohibited, 4) **Retention**: Emails are retained for 7 years per legal requirements — do not assume deleted emails are gone, 5) **External sharing**: Do not forward company emails to personal email accounts (violates data security), 6) **Appropriate personal use**: Brief, infrequent personal messages (doctor appointment confirmation, family emergency coordination) are acceptable, 7) **Inappropriate personal use**: Running a side business, sending offensive content, personal newsletters, chain letters — results in disciplinary action, 8) **Upon separation**: Email account is deactivated — set up auto-reply directing senders to your personal email before leaving. Company email is company property — use it professionally and primarily for business.

prompt: Can I take leave for my own wedding?
chosen: Wedding leave policy: 1) **Standard leave**: Use accrued leave (casual or earned) for your wedding and honeymoon — typically 5-10 days depending on your leave balance, 2) **Company wedding benefit**: One-time $1,000 wedding gift (if married while employed) — request through Benefits portal with marriage certificate, 3) **Flexible scheduling**: If you need additional time beyond accrued leave, discuss unpaid leave or flexible schedule with manager — weddings are significant life events, 4) **Colleague invitations**: Inviting coworkers to your wedding is personal — no pressure or obligation; no manager-led collections for wedding gifts, 5) **Time off for planning**: Wedding planning should occur outside work hours; excessive personal calls/appointments during work may require use of accrued leave, 6) **Same-sex marriage**: Fully recognized and supported — same benefits apply regardless of gender, 7) **Documentation**: Marriage certificate may be required for benefits updates (adding spouse to health insurance, changing emergency contacts), 8) **Return to work**: No special accommodations upon return — standard re-entry. Congratulations on your wedding! The company supports work-life balance for major life events.

prompt: What is the policy on employees volunteering as mentors outside the company?
chosen: External mentoring and volunteering policy: 1) **Personal time**: Mentoring outside organizations (schools, nonprofits, youth programs) on personal time is encouraged — no disclosure required, 2) **Company-sponsored mentoring**: Company partners with organizations (Big Brothers Big Sisters, Year Up, coding bootcamps) — volunteer through CSR portal, 3) **VTO hours**: Up to 16 hours/year of Volunteer Time Off (paid) can be used for external mentoring, 4) **Company representation**: If mentoring as a company representative (company-sponsored program), you may mention your employer; if mentoring personally, clarify it's your individual capacity, 5) **Conflicts**: Cannot mentor employees of competitors or clients using company knowledge — disclose if uncertain, 6) **Liability**: Company's insurance does not cover external mentoring activities — you're acting as an individual, 7) **Time**: External mentoring during work hours requires manager approval and use of accrued leave or VTO, 8) **Recognition**: External mentoring is valued in performance reviews (demonstrates leadership, community engagement) — include in your annual self-assessment. The company encourages employees to give back through mentoring and community service.

prompt: Can I request a copy of all my performance reviews?
chosen: Performance review access policy: 1) **Current reviews**: Access all performance reviews through HR portal > My Performance > Review History — includes self-assessments, manager reviews, and peer feedback, 2) **Historical reviews**: Reviews from previous systems (before current HR portal) are archived — request from HR (provided within 5 business days), 3) **Format**: Reviews are provided as PDFs with original signatures and dates, 4) **Disputes**: If you believe a review contains factual errors, submit written correction request to HR within 30 days — manager reviews and HR decides on correction, 5) **Confidentiality**: Performance reviews are confidential — sharing them externally (with recruiters, on social media) may violate confidentiality policy, 6) **Use for appeals**: Reviews may be used as evidence in promotion appeals, grievance procedures, or discrimination claims, 7) **Retention**: Company retains performance reviews for duration of employment plus 7 years (legal requirement), 8) **Post-separation**: Former employees may request copies of their reviews for up to 3 years after separation (for job applications, graduate school). Performance reviews are your record — keep personal copies for your career development.

prompt: What is the company's policy on employees creating open-source projects?
chosen: Open-source project policy: 1) **Personal projects**: You may create and contribute to open-source projects on personal time using personal equipment — no disclosure required unless project creates conflict, 2) **Company-related projects**: If open-source project relates to company business, uses company knowledge, or could compete with company products, disclose to Legal — company may claim ownership or request collaboration, 3) **Company-sponsored open-source**: Company encourages open-sourcing non-proprietary tools (internal utilities, frameworks) — submit proposal to Engineering Leadership, 4) **IP ownership**: Personal open-source projects belong to you; company-sponsored projects are owned by company but released under open-source license (MIT, Apache, GPL), 5) **Time**: Personal open-source work must occur outside work hours; company open-source work during work hours requires manager approval, 6) **Conflicts**: Cannot open-source company code, trade secrets, or proprietary algorithms — violations may result in termination, 7) **Recognition**: Open-source contributions are valued in performance reviews (technical expertise, community engagement) — include in self-assessment, 8) **Licensing**: If releasing personal project under open-source license, ensure you own all code (no company code included). The company supports open-source culture while protecting intellectual property.

prompt: Can I take leave for a family emergency (not medical)?

prompt: What is the policy on employees accepting board positions at for-profit companies?
chosen: For-profit board service policy: 1) **External boards**: Serving on boards of for-profit companies (other than your employer) is considered outside employment and requires disclosure and approval, 2) **Approval process**: Submit board service details to HR > Outside Activities with: company name, role (director, advisor, officer), time commitment, compensation, and potential conflicts, 3) **Conflicts**: Cannot serve on boards of: company competitors, company clients/vendors (if you have decision authority), startups using company IP, 4) **Time commitment**: Board service typically requires 10-20 hours/month — must not interfere with primary job responsibilities, 5) **Compensation**: Board compensation (cash, stock options) is yours to keep but must be reported annually (tax and conflict of interest purposes), 6) **Fiduciary duty**: As a board member, you have legal obligations to the company — ensure these don't conflict with your employer's interests, 7) **Company resources**: Cannot use company time, equipment, or staff for board activities, 8) **Liability**: Company's D&O insurance does not cover external board service — you're personally liable (board may provide indemnification). Board service at for-profit companies creates potential conflicts — approval is not guaranteed and is assessed case-by-case.

prompt: Can I get a letter verifying my income for a mortgage?
chosen: Income verification for mortgage/loans: 1) **Standard verification**: Submit request through HR portal > Document Requests > Income Verification — specifies lender name, loan type, and required information, 2) **Information provided**: Employment dates, job title, base salary, bonus history (if applicable), employment status (active), and likelihood of continued employment, 3) **Processing time**: 3-5 business days for standard requests; 24-48 hours for urgent (with documented closing date), 4) **Format**: Letter is on company letterhead, signed by HR, addressed to the lender (not to you), 5) **Additional documents**: Lenders may request: recent pay stubs (download from Payroll portal), W-2 forms (from your records), tax returns (your responsibility), 6) **Self-employed contractors**: Income verification is provided by your agency or client — contact them directly, 7) **Bonus/commission**: Variable compensation is verified with historical data (past 2 years) — lenders understand it's not guaranteed, 8) **No fee**: Income verification is provided at no cost to employees. Mortgage applications often have tight deadlines — submit verification request as soon as you start the loan process.
